openings.domain: Acoustic metamaterial unit cells for subwavelength sound absorption
openings.verifier: k-Wave (MATLAB/Python FDTD acoustics simulator) — simulate transmission loss and absorption coefficient for a given 3D unit cell geometry; run time < 1 hour per candidate on a laptop
openings.search_space: Continuous geometry of Helmholtz-resonator-like cavities with branching channels, parameterized by 10+ dimensions (neck length, cavity volume, taper angle, porous lining thickness, etc.)
openings.neglect_reason: Most acoustic metamaterial research is hand-tuned or uses simple parameter sweeps; big labs focus on photonic or phononic crystals with more funding.
openings.alien_example: A fractal tree of nested quarter-wave resonators that achieves >90% absorption from 200–800 Hz in a 2 cm thick panel — a shape no human would intuitively design.
openings.why_now: k-Wave is mature, open-source, and fast on CPU; cheap 3D printing of polymer prototypes allows quick validation.

openings.domain: Passive RFID tag antenna topologies for ultra-narrowband backscatter
openings.verifier: openEMS (open-source FDTD EM simulator) — compute S11, gain, and radar cross-section at 868/915 MHz; run time < 30 min per candidate on a workstation
openings.search_space: 2.5D planar meander-line and slot geometries on thin flexible substrate, with >50 free parameters (trace width, spacing, number of turns, loading stubs, ground-plane cuts)
openings.neglect_reason: RFID antenna design is considered a solved commodity; big labs chase 5G/mmWave phased arrays. The niche of ultra-low-cost, narrowband tags is ignored.
openings.alien_example: A non-intuitive spiral-slot hybrid that achieves 10 MHz bandwidth at 915 MHz with 3 dBi gain on a 2 cm × 2 cm footprint — looks like a distorted asterisk.
openings.why_now: openEMS runs on a gaming laptop; tape-on-paper prototyping costs < $1 per iteration.

openings.domain: Topology-optimized heat sink fins for natural convection in enclosed spaces
openings.verifier: ElmerFEM (open-source FEA) — conjugate heat transfer simulation (laminar flow + conduction) for a given 3D fin shape; run time < 2 hours per candidate on a workstation
openings.search_space: 3D voxel or level-set representation of fin geometry within a 50×50×20 mm bounding box, with porosity, branching, and surface area constraints
openings.neglect_reason: Big labs optimize heat sinks for forced convection (servers, EVs) with expensive CFD solvers; natural convection in consumer electronics is considered low-priority.
openings.alien_example: A dendritic 'coral' structure with variable-thickness branches that doubles heat transfer vs. straight fins at the same mass — resembles a miniature tree skeleton.
openings.why_now: ElmerFEM is free and parallel; 3D metal printing (SLM) is now affordable for one-off prototypes.

openings.domain: Microfluidic droplet generator junction geometries for monodisperse emulsions
openings.verifier: OpenFOAM interFoam (VOF multiphase solver) — simulate droplet formation at a T-junction or flow-focusing geometry; run time < 4 hours per candidate on a workstation
openings.search_space: 2D or 2.5D channel cross-section shapes (rounded, triangular, stepped, with grooves or pillars) parameterized by 8+ continuous and discrete variables
openings.neglect_reason: Microfluidics is fragmented; big labs focus on organ-on-chip or DNA analysis, not basic droplet generation geometry. Most papers use hand-drawn designs.
openings.alien_example: An asymmetric double-step junction that produces 20 μm droplets at 10 kHz with CV < 1% — a shape that looks like a broken keyhole.
openings.why_now: OpenFOAM is free; soft lithography molds can be 3D-printed cheaply for validation.

openings.domain: Compact optical freeform lens arrays for uniform LED illumination
openings.verifier: RayOpt (open-source ray tracer, e.g., Python ray-tracing with PyOptica or OASYS) — compute irradiance uniformity on a target plane for a given lens surface; run time < 10 min per candidate on a laptop
openings.search_space: B-spline or NURBS control points defining a 2D array of freeform lenslets (5×5 to 20×20), each with 6–10 degrees of freedom, plus pitch and offset
openings.neglect_reason: Big optics labs design for lithography or astronomy; LED lighting optics are considered low-tech and solved by simple diffusers.
openings.alien_example: A non-periodic array of asymmetric 'saddle' lenslets that achieves 95% uniformity over a 1:4 aspect ratio rectangle — no two lenslets are identical.
openings.why_now: Ray tracing is trivial on a laptop; 3D-printed lens arrays from clear resin are cheap.

openings.domain: Scheduling of multi-stage batch chemical reactions with shared resources
openings.verifier: CP-SAT solver (OR-Tools) — given a candidate schedule (order and resource assignment), compute makespan, resource conflicts, and feasibility; run time < 1 min per candidate on a laptop
openings.search_space: Permutation of task order across 10–30 batches on 3–5 reactors with 2 shared utilities (e.g., heating/cooling), each batch having 4–8 sequential steps with variable durations
openings.neglect_reason: Scheduling research focuses on job-shop or flow-shop for manufacturing; chemical batch scheduling is highly domain-specific and neglected by AI labs.
openings.alien_example: A schedule that interleaves steps from different batches on the same reactor in a non-obvious 'zigzag' pattern, reducing total makespan by 30% vs. human heuristic.
openings.why_now: OR-Tools CP-SAT is free and fast; chemical plants need better scheduling for flexible manufacturing.

openings.domain: Topology-optimized compliant mechanisms for micro-positioning stages
openings.verifier: CalculiX (open-source FEA) — compute displacement, stress, and parasitic motion for a given 2D planar topology under input force; run time < 30 min per candidate on a laptop
openings.search_space: Binary or grayscale pixel grid (e.g., 100×100) representing material distribution, with symmetry and connectivity constraints
openings.neglect_reason: Compliant mechanism design is a classic TO problem, but big labs focus on aerospace-scale or biomedical implants; micro-positioning (e.g., for fiber alignment) is a tiny niche.
openings.alien_example: A 'spiderweb' topology with curved flexures that achieves 100:1 displacement amplification with zero lateral drift — looks like a distorted Celtic knot.
openings.why_now: CalculiX runs on a laptop; wire EDM or 3D printing can fabricate steel prototypes cheaply.

openings.domain: RF/WiFi
openings.signal: WiFi CSI (Channel State Information) amplitude/phase perturbations
openings.sensor: Intel 5300 WiFi card with modified driver ($20-30)
openings.coupling: Human respiration and heartbeat cause sub-mm chest movements that modulate the multipath reflections of WiFi signals, altering CSI subcarrier phases via Doppler shifts and path-length changes.
openings.verifier: Simultaneous recording with a chest-worn Polar H10 ECG/HR strap ($50); cross-correlate CSI-derived breathing rate and HRV peaks with ground truth from the strap
openings.constructive_use: Non-contact sleep apnea screening, athlete recovery monitoring, or stress detection without wearables (consent-only)
openings.neglect_reason: Most WiFi sensing research targets people surveillance or gesture recognition; no cheap, open-source self-diagnostic tool exists using $30 hardware
openings.alien_example: A bedside ESP32 with CSI sniffing that detects your breathing pattern and adjusts room humidity via a smart humidifier to prevent snoring

openings.domain: Vibration
openings.signal: Low-frequency structural vibrations (10-500 Hz) from machinery
openings.sensor: Piezoelectric contact mic glued to a $5 stethoscope chest piece
openings.coupling: Bearing faults or gear wear create impact-induced resonant vibrations that propagate through metal housings; the contact mic converts these into audio signals with distinct spectral signatures (e.g., sidebands at shaft rotation frequency)
openings.verifier: Disassemble the machine after recording and visually inspect bearings for pitting or spalling; compare vibration spectrogram features to actual damage
openings.constructive_use: Predictive maintenance for home appliances (washing machines, drills, pumps) before catastrophic failure
openings.neglect_reason: Industrial vibration analysis uses $1000+ accelerometers; no one has built a <$10 contact-mic rig that logs to a phone for consumer machinery
openings.alien_example: A DIY 'ear trumpet' that listens to your fridge compressor and texts you 'defrost me' 3 days before ice buildup stalls the fan

openings.domain: Acoustic
openings.signal: Airborne sound from water leaks in pipes
openings.sensor: Phone microphone (any smartphone)
openings.coupling: Pressurized water escaping a pinhole leak creates turbulent flow noise (500-2000 Hz) that propagates through pipe walls and into room air; the sound's frequency and amplitude correlate with leak size and pressure
openings.verifier: Inject a controlled leak using a needle valve on a test pipe; measure actual flow rate with a graduated cylinder and stopwatch; compare with audio RMS and spectral centroid
openings.constructive_use: Early detection of hidden pipe leaks in walls before water damage occurs, using only a phone app
openings.neglect_reason: Commercial leak detectors use ultrasonic sensors or thermal cameras; no simple acoustic phone app has been validated for sub-1 L/min leaks in residential pipes
openings.alien_example: A spider-like robot that crawls along baseboards with a phone mic, mapping leak locations by sound triangulation

openings.domain: Optical/Light
openings.signal: Ambient light flicker from AC mains (100/120 Hz)
openings.sensor: Photodiode + audio jack input on a phone (total <$5)
openings.coupling: LED bulbs driven by cheap rectifiers have 100 Hz (Europe) or 120 Hz (US) intensity ripple; the exact frequency shifts proportionally with grid frequency, which varies with generator load. A failing transformer or overloaded grid causes micro-hertz deviations
openings.verifier: Plug a calibrated frequency counter (e.g., GPS-locked OCXO) into the same wall outlet; compare photodiode-derived grid frequency with counter reading
openings.constructive_use: Grid frequency monitoring for renewable integration studies or detecting power plant instability before blackouts
openings.neglect_reason: Grid monitoring uses expensive PMUs (Phasor Measurement Units); a photodiode plugged into a phone is absurdly cheap but nobody has built the app
openings.alien_example: A sunflower-shaped photodiode array that 'listens' to grid frequency and predicts local brownouts by detecting frequency droop patterns

openings.domain: EM
openings.signal: Magnetic field from DC motor brush arcing
openings.sensor: Coil of 100 turns of wire (salvaged from a relay) + phone mic input (induction pickup)
openings.coupling: Worn brushes on a DC motor create intermittent arcing that generates broadband electromagnetic pulses (1-100 MHz); the coil detects these as voltage spikes, which when rectified produce a crackling audio signal whose rate equals brush-passing frequency
openings.verifier: Disconnect motor, inspect brush length with calipers; compare arcing rate (from recorded audio) to predicted rate from RPM and commutator segments
openings.constructive_use: Non-invasive brush wear monitoring for power tools, RC motors, or robot vacuums without disassembly
openings.neglect_reason: Brush wear detection uses Hall sensors or current shunt measurements; a simple coil pickup is overlooked despite being cheaper and easier
openings.alien_example: A 'spark sniffer' that clips onto a drill's power cord and tells you 'replace brushes in 12 hours' based on arcing trend

openings.domain: Power
openings.signal: Power supply ripple from electrolytic capacitor aging
openings.sensor: 0.1 µF capacitor in series with phone mic (AC coupling) + voltage divider
openings.coupling: Aging electrolytic caps lose capacitance and increase ESR, causing increased 100/120 Hz ripple on DC power rails; the ripple amplitude is proportional to ESR rise, which is a known failure precursor
openings.verifier: Desolder the capacitor and measure its capacitance and ESR with an LCR meter; compare ripple amplitude (recorded via phone) to actual degradation
openings.constructive_use: Predictive failure detection for power supplies in PCs, monitors, or audio amplifiers before they fail and damage other components
openings.neglect_reason: Capacitor testing requires desoldering or expensive ESR meters; no one has used a phone's audio input as a ripple detector for DIY diagnostics
openings.alien_example: A 'cap whisperer' probe that plugs into a PC's 12V rail and plays a tone whose pitch rises as the capacitor ages, warning you to replace it

openings.domain: Thermal
openings.signal: Infrared emission from thermal bridge in building insulation
openings.sensor: MLX90614 IR thermometer ($10) pointed at wall, read by Arduino
openings.coupling: A missing or wet insulation section creates a thermal bridge: the wall surface temperature differs from surrounding areas by 1-5°C depending on outdoor temperature difference and insulation R-value; IR sensor detects this as a spatial temperature gradient
openings.verifier: Drill a small hole, insert a borescope, and visually confirm insulation void or moisture; compare with IR scan pattern
openings.constructive_use: Low-cost home energy audit to find heat loss locations without a $500 thermal camera
openings.neglect_reason: Thermal cameras are the standard; a single-point IR sensor scanned across a wall is crude but nobody has automated the scanning and interpolation to produce a thermal map
openings.alien_example: A Roomba-like robot that drags an IR sensor across your baseboards, building a thermal map of your house and pointing out cold spots with a laser pointer

openings.domain: adaptive traffic signal control for grid networks
openings.strategy_space: phase-splitting policies, offset patterns, cycle-length schedules for multiple intersections under varying demand
openings.simulator: SUMO (Simulation of Urban MObility) with a 4x4 grid scenario; a candidate policy is run for 10 simulated minutes and average wait time per vehicle is returned in <30 seconds on a laptop
openings.value_if_found: reducing average travel time by 15-30% over fixed-time or actuated control, with immediate deployment in city traffic systems
openings.neglect_reason: most traffic RL work uses synthetic single-intersection environments or complex multi-agent setups; cheap SUMO grid search for novel phase-timing heuristics is underexplored
openings.alien_example: a policy that uses only the ratio of queue lengths on perpendicular approaches to decide whether to skip a phase entirely, combined with a 'green wave' offset learned via random search

openings.domain: TCP congestion control for lossy satellite links
openings.strategy_space: parameters of a delay-based or hybrid congestion window update rule (e.g., thresholds, growth factors, backoff multipliers) and binary decisions like 'use ECN feedback or not'
openings.simulator: ns-3 with a satellite link model (high delay, 1% random loss); a candidate TCP variant runs 2 simulated file transfers and reports average throughput and fairness index in <1 minute on a laptop
openings.value_if_found: 10-40% throughput improvement over CUBIC or BBR in high-loss-delay environments, critical for Starlink/OneWeb performance
openings.neglect_reason: ns-3 TCP research focuses on detailed protocol modifications or ML-based control, not cheap random search over simple heuristics for niche link types
openings.alien_example: a rule that increases cwnd by 3 MSS per RTT when loss rate <0.5%, but halves it on each loss only if RTT > 200ms, else cuts by 0.3

openings.domain: packet routing in mesh networks with intermittent links
openings.strategy_space: forwarding rules based on link-layer metrics (expected transmission count, signal strength, recent success rate) and time-dependent backoff windows for retransmission
openings.simulator: ns-3 with a 20-node random mesh topology and a simple mobility model that drops links 10% of the time; a candidate routing heuristic is scored by average packet delivery ratio over 200 packets in <30 seconds
openings.value_if_found: 30-50% higher delivery ratio than OLSR or BATMAN in lossy meshes, applicable to IoT and community networks
openings.neglect_reason: mesh routing research uses complex protocols (HWMP, B.A.T.M.A.N. advanced) or ML; cheap heuristic search over simple forwarding rules is ignored
openings.alien_example: a rule: 'if ETX>3 and signal strength<-75dBm, forward via the neighbor with the lowest recent RTT, else via the one with highest delivery ratio in last 10 seconds'

openings.domain: auction bid shading for repeated ad slot auctions
openings.strategy_space: bid multipliers as a function of auction characteristics (number of bidders, reserve price, ad position) and a 'shading' rule that interpolates between truthful and competitive bids
openings.simulator: a Python discrete-event market replay using the real AdX dataset (or synthetic bid distributions); a candidate shading policy is evaluated over 1000 auctions for average profit (utility minus payment) in <10 seconds
openings.value_if_found: 5-15% increase in advertiser surplus without reducing win rate, directly monetizable in programmatic advertising
openings.neglect_reason: most bid shading research uses analytical solutions or complex RL; cheap heuristic search over simple parametric families is underexplored for the second-price auction case
openings.alien_example: shade by 0.7*reserve_price/expected_second_bid when number of bidders >5, else bid truthfully; adjust shade linearly with ad position index

openings.domain: resource allocation for shared last-mile delivery fleets
openings.strategy_space: priority rules for assigning parcels to vehicles (e.g., by deadline, size, distance from depot) and dynamic rebalancing thresholds (when to return to depot vs continue)
openings.simulator: a custom discrete-event simulation in Python (or SUMO with delivery agents) for 100 parcels and 5 vehicles over 8 hours; a candidate policy is scored by total cost (fuel + missed-delivery penalties) in <1 minute
openings.value_if_found: 10-20% cost reduction over FIFO or nearest-first heuristics, applicable to Uber Direct, Amazon Flex
openings.neglect_reason: delivery fleet research focuses on mixed-integer programming or deep RL; cheap heuristic search over simple priority rules for dynamic assignment is overlooked
openings.alien_example: assign parcels with >2h deadline to the vehicle with highest remaining capacity; for urgent parcels, use a rule: 'if distance to next parcel < 0.5km, assign the one with smallest slack time'

openings.domain: evolutionary crossover and mutation operators for symbolic regression
openings.strategy_space: parameters of a GP system: crossover point selection bias (e.g., depth-weighted), mutation rate schedule, and a rule for when to replace parents with offspring (e.g., tournament size, elitism fraction)
openings.simulator: a Python evolutionary framework (e.g., DEAP) running on 10 benchmark symbolic regression problems (e.g., Nguyen-1 to Nguyen-10); a candidate operator set is scored by average best fitness over 20 generations in <30 seconds
openings.value_if_found: faster convergence to simpler expressions, reducing overfitting and improving interpretability; useful for scientific discovery
openings.neglect_reason: GP research focuses on new representation or advanced operators; cheap parameter search over classic operator variants for symbolic regression is neglected in favor of deep learning
openings.alien_example: crossover always swaps subtrees at depth 2-4 (avoiding root and leaves); mutation rate = 0.1 * (1 - generation/100); replacement uses tournament size 3 only if offspring fitness > parent fitness * 0.95

openings.domain: PCB component placement for thermal uniformity
openings.objective: minimize maximum temperature gradient across board + peak temperature (evaluated via fast steady-state thermal resistance network solver, ~0.01s per placement)
openings.space: 10^200+ (50-200 components, each with 6 DOF rotation+mirror, multiple board layers)
openings.value_if_solved: $2B/yr savings in cooling hardware, reliability gains, smaller enclosures for power electronics/telecom
openings.neglect_reason: PCB EDA tools focus on electrical routing; thermal analysis is post-layout simulation, not optimization. Academic work uses slow FEM, not cheap surrogate objectives
openings.alien_example: Place high-power GaN FETs in a Fibonacci spiral pattern, interleaved with low-power passives, to create counter-rotating heat convection cells

openings.domain: Multi-robot shelf-to-order picking in dark warehouses with heterogeneous item shapes
openings.objective: minimize total robot travel time + shelf swap count (evaluated via discrete event simulation, ~0.05s per schedule for 1000 orders)
openings.space: 10^500+ (assigning 10^4 items from 10^3 shelves to 50 robots over 8-hour shift)
openings.value_if_solved: $5B/yr in warehouse OPEX reduction (Amazon/Alibaba scale), 30% throughput increase
openings.neglect_reason: Industry uses greedy heuristics or generic VRP solvers; academic work assumes uniform item sizes or ignores shelf repositioning time
openings.alien_example: Use prime-number modulo hashing of item IDs to dynamically cluster orders into 'galaxy' groups that minimize shelf contention

openings.domain: 3D bin packing of irregular surgical instrument sets into sterilization trays
openings.objective: maximize packing density + minimize instrument contact (scratch risk) via fast voxel overlap check (~0.001s per candidate)
openings.space: 10^100+ (20-50 instruments with 6 DOF each, convex hull approximation, tray size constraints)
openings.value_if_solved: $500M/yr in reduced instrument damage, faster sterilization cycle, fewer emergency surgeries delayed
openings.neglect_reason: Hospital logistics uses manual packing or simple 2D nesting; academic 3D packing assumes cuboids or known CAD models
openings.alien_example: Pack instruments in a 'Fibonacci sphere' arrangement where each tool's handle points toward a central drainage axis

openings.domain: Satellite ground station antenna scheduling with weather-dependent link margins
openings.objective: maximize total downloaded data (bits) minus penalty for missed priority passes (evaluated via fast link budget calculator, ~0.001s per schedule)
openings.space: 10^300+ (50 satellites × 10 ground stations × 1000 passes/day, 1-minute scheduling granularity)
openings.value_if_solved: $1B/yr in satellite operator revenue (more data downlinked), reduced ground infrastructure cost
openings.neglect_reason: Current schedulers use simple greedy or constraint propagation; weather effects are handled reactively, not optimized preemptively
openings.alien_example: Treat each satellite pass as a 'musical chairs' token auction where stations bid based on cloud cover forecast, resolved via stable marriage algorithm

openings.domain: Hospital nurse shift assignment with circadian rhythm preference learning
openings.objective: minimize weighted sum of preference violations + shift continuity breaks (evaluated via linear programming relaxation, ~0.02s per assignment for 100 nurses)
openings.space: 10^150+ (100 nurses × 28 days × 3 shifts, with 5 preference categories each)
openings.value_if_solved: $3B/yr in reduced nurse burnout, turnover, and medical errors (US hospitals alone)
openings.neglect_reason: Hospital scheduling uses seniority-based manual assignment or generic rostering software; no model learns individual circadian preferences from past satisfaction
openings.alien_example: Assign shifts using a 'honeybee waggle dance' algorithm where nurses vote on schedules via anonymous preference tokens that decay with circadian misalignment

openings.domain: Street-level last-mile delivery route optimization with dynamic parking availability
openings.objective: minimize total driver walking distance + parking search time (evaluated via graph shortest-path with congestion penalty, ~0.01s per route for 200 stops)
openings.space: 10^400+ (200 delivery points × 50 parking spots each, time-dependent availability)
openings.value_if_solved: $10B/yr in delivery cost savings (FedEx/UPS scale), reduced double-parking fines and emissions
openings.neglect_reason: Route optimization assumes curb-side parking always available; academic work ignores the walk from parking to delivery point as a decision variable
openings.alien_example: Pre-position 'parking satellites' where one driver parks a cargo bike while a second driver walks a loop, swapping via rendezvous points

openings.domain: Acoustic metamaterial unit cells for subwavelength sound focusing
openings.verifier: k-Wave: time-domain acoustic simulation; score on focusing gain vs. side-lobe level at target frequency
openings.search_space: Continuous geometry of 3D-printable labyrinthine channels within a 1cm³ unit cell (wall thickness, channel width, number of turns, taper angle) × 10⁴⁰+ combos
openings.neglect_reason: Most work uses hand-tuned Helmholtz resonators or simple split-ring shapes; generative search over arbitrary channel topologies unexplored
openings.alien_example: A chiral 'double-spiral' with 3 interleaved channels that creates a 15dB focal spot at λ/20, looking like a microscopic ammonite fossil

openings.domain: Passive acoustic diode structures via nonlinear scattering
openings.verifier: k-Wave with nonlinear solver: compute rectification ratio (forward transmission / reverse transmission) for finite-amplitude waves
openings.search_space: 2D arrangement of air-filled cavities in water, each cavity defined by (radius, neck length, offset) in a periodic lattice; ~10²⁰ configurations
openings.neglect_reason: Acoustic diodes typically use active electronics or phononic crystals with simple defects; nonlinear passive designs with multiple cavities unexplored by generative search
openings.alien_example: A 'ratchet' pattern of 7 asymmetric cavities that transmits 80% of 10kPa incident wave but blocks 95% in reverse, resembling a distorted honeycomb

openings.domain: Broadband acoustic carpet cloak for underwater sonar avoidance
openings.verifier: k-Wave: 2D pressure field comparison between cloaked object and free field; score on scattering cross-section reduction over 5-50kHz
openings.search_space: Layered gradient-index structure with 20-200 layers, each layer having (thickness, density, speed-of-sound) from printable metamaterials; ~10³⁰ combos
openings.neglect_reason: Most acoustic cloaks target single frequencies or narrow bands; broadband designs rely on analytical solutions, not generative discovery
openings.alien_example: A 15-layer 'onion' with alternating stiff/soft helical windings that reduces scattering by 20dB across 2 octaves, looking like a transparent sea urchin

openings.domain: Acoustic black hole (ABH) termination shapes for vibration damping
openings.verifier: Elmer FEM: 2D plate vibration eigenmodes + forced response; score on reflection coefficient at beam end
openings.search_space: 1D thickness profile along beam length: polynomial coefficients, power-law exponents, sinusoidal modulations, discrete step patterns; ~10¹⁵ combos
openings.neglect_reason: ABH designs follow power-law tapers; non-monotonic or oscillatory profiles never systematically explored
openings.alien_example: A 'caterpillar' profile with 5 alternating thick/thin segments that achieves -40dB reflection at 200Hz, looking like a ribbed worm

openings.domain: Coupled Helmholtz resonator arrays for low-frequency sound absorption
openings.verifier: k-Wave: plane wave tube simulation; score on absorption coefficient α > 0.9 at 50-200Hz
openings.search_space: Array of 4-16 resonators, each with (neck diameter, cavity volume, position offset); plus interconnecting tube geometry; ~10²⁵ configurations
openings.neglect_reason: Existing designs use identical resonators or simple series coupling; generative search over heterogeneous coupling topologies absent
openings.alien_example: A 'spiderweb' of 7 resonators connected by thin capillaries that absorbs 95% at 80Hz with total thickness λ/50, resembling a microscopic lung

openings.domain: Optimal microphone array layouts for acoustic beamforming
openings.verifier: Python acoustic simulation (pyroomacoustics): compute directivity index and side-lobe level for given array geometry
openings.search_space: Positions of 8-32 microphones on a 2D plane (continuous coordinates) with symmetry constraints; ~10⁴⁰ layouts
openings.neglect_reason: Arrays use regular grids, random sparse arrays, or spiral layouts; generative search over non-intuitive asymmetric clusters unexplored
openings.alien_example: A 'broken ring' of 12 mics arranged like a distorted daisy that achieves -35dB sidelobes with only 12 elements, looking like a partial snowflake

openings.domain: Acoustic Fresnel zone plates for air-coupled ultrasound focusing
openings.verifier: k-Wave: 2D axisymmetric simulation; score on focal pressure relative to plane wave input
openings.search_space: Binary (opaque/transparent) annular ring pattern with 5-50 rings, each ring having (inner radius, outer radius, phase shift material thickness); ~10²⁰ combos
openings.neglect_reason: Standard Fresnel plates use half-wave zones; non-integer zone boundaries, multiple phase levels, and asymmetric patterns unexplored
openings.alien_example: A 'Fibonacci spiral' zone plate with 23 non-concentric rings that focuses at 3 different depths simultaneously, looking like a fingerprint

openings.domain: Acoustic metasurface for anomalous reflection with minimal parasitic scattering
openings.verifier: k-Wave: far-field pressure pattern; score on ratio of energy redirected to target angle vs. other angles
openings.search_space: Array of 10-100 subwavelength unit cells, each cell having (cavity depth, neck width, number of internal partitions); ~10³⁰ configurations
openings.neglect_reason: Metasurfaces use linear phase gradients; generative search over non-local, coupled unit cells with phase-amplitude tradeoffs absent
openings.alien_example: A 'fractal' arrangement of 64 cells that redirects 90% of incident energy to 60° with only 2% parasitic lobes, looking like a Menger sponge slice

openings.domain: Structural vibration / loose joint detection
openings.signal: Low-frequency vibration (<500 Hz) from wind or foot traffic
openings.sensor: Smartphone accelerometer (MEMS, 3-axis, ~$0.50 part cost)
openings.coupling: Loose bolts or degraded joints in a metal-frame structure (e.g., scaffolding, bridge railing, shipping container) create nonlinear rattling. The acceleration signal shows intermittent high-amplitude spikes and subharmonic peaks not present in a rigid joint. The loose interface modulates the structure's natural frequency by changing effective stiffness during each cycle.
openings.verifier: Ground truth: torque wrench + feeler gauge measurement of bolt tightness. Check: record 30 s of idle vibration, compute RMS + spectral kurtosis, compare against known-tight baseline from same structure.
openings.constructive_use: Preventive maintenance of temporary structures (stages, grandstands, scaffolding) without installing dedicated sensors — use a passerby's phone pressed against a beam.
openings.neglect_reason: Most structural monitoring uses expensive accelerometers or strain gauges; phone-grade MEMS considered too noisy. Nobody has calibrated phone vibration against bolt torque in a controlled field test.
openings.alien_example: A construction foreman taps a phone against a scaffold pole; the phone buzzes once and displays 'Joint 3: 60% residual torque — tighten before loading.'

openings.domain: Power line / transformer mechanical state
openings.signal: Mains hum (50/60 Hz) and its harmonics (100-500 Hz) radiating as acoustic pressure
openings.sensor: Contact microphone (piezo disc, ~$2) clamped to the transformer housing or pole
openings.coupling: Laminated core delamination or winding looseness changes the magnetostrictive strain pattern, altering the amplitude ratio of even vs. odd harmonics of the mains hum. A healthy transformer produces strong 100 Hz (2f), weak 150 Hz (3f); loosening increases 3f/2f ratio by >5 dB due to asymmetric flux paths.
openings.verifier: Ground truth: winding resistance measurement + dissolved gas analysis from oil sample. Check: record 10 s of contact audio, compute FFT, extract 100/150 Hz peak ratio, compare to lab-tested threshold.
openings.constructive_use: Low-cost condition monitoring of distribution transformers in remote substations — attach a piezo disc and an ESP32, report anomaly via LoRa.
openings.neglect_reason: Acoustic monitoring of transformers uses expensive ultrasonic microphones or vibration analyzers; nobody has characterized the simple 3f/2f ratio from a $2 piezo against winding looseness.
openings.alien_example: A lineman places a suction-cup mic on a pole transformer; the device chirps '3f excess — internal looseness detected. Recommend oil test within 30 days.'

openings.domain: Structural vibration / concrete crack detection
openings.signal: Impact-echo acoustic response (1-10 kHz) after a controlled tap
openings.sensor: Smartphone microphone (MEMS, ~$0.15) held against the concrete surface
openings.coupling: A surface-breaking crack in concrete creates a distinct low-frequency resonance (typically 2-5 kHz) compared to intact concrete (8-15 kHz) because the crack acts as a thin, air-filled cavity that lowers the local stiffness. The frequency shift scales with crack depth: deeper crack → lower resonance.
openings.verifier: Ground truth: crack width/depth measured with a microscope and feeler gauge. Check: tap a coin 5 cm from crack, record 0.5 s audio, compute peak frequency via autocorrelation, compare to calibration curve from known cracks.
openings.constructive_use: Rapid sidewalk/bridge deck inspection by a single worker tapping with a coin and reading frequency from a phone app — no expensive ultrasonic equipment needed.
openings.neglect_reason: Impact-echo is a known NDT technique but uses dedicated piezoelectric transducers and signal generators. Phone microphone considered too low-fidelity for the 1-10 kHz range; nobody has shown it works with just a coin tap and phone mic.
openings.alien_example: A city inspector taps a curb with a quarter; the phone says 'Crack detected, depth ~8 mm. Priority: medium.'

openings.domain: Pipe vibration / water leak localization
openings.signal: Structure-borne acoustic noise (50-500 Hz) from turbulent flow through a leak orifice
openings.sensor: Contact microphone (piezo disc) or smartphone accelerometer pressed against the pipe
openings.coupling: Water escaping a pinhole leak generates broadband acoustic noise centered at a frequency inversely proportional to leak diameter (f ≈ c / d, where c ≈ 1500 m/s in water, so a 1 mm leak → ~1.5 kHz but structure-borne coupling shifts it to 100-500 Hz). The signal amplitude decays with distance from leak, and cross-correlation between two sensor positions gives time delay → leak location.
openings.verifier: Ground truth: locate leak by visual inspection or dye test after excavation. Check: place two sensors 10 m apart, record 60 s, compute cross-correlation peak lag, convert to distance using wave speed measured by a known tap.
openings.constructive_use: Detect and locate water leaks in buried municipal pipes using only two cheap contact mics and a smartphone — no acoustic correlator rental ($500/day).
openings.neglect_reason: Correlators exist but are expensive dedicated devices; nobody has demonstrated a DIY phone-based correlator with piezo discs that achieves <1 m accuracy on real buried pipes.
openings.alien_example: A plumber clamps two clips on exposed basement pipes, runs a phone app, and sees 'Leak at 4.2 m from sensor A. Dig here.'

openings.domain: Window / glass pane structural integrity
openings.signal: Acoustic resonance of a glass pane excited by ambient noise or a finger tap
openings.sensor: Smartphone microphone placed against the glass (with suction cup adapter)
openings.coupling: A cracked or weakened glass pane shows a lower fundamental resonance frequency and higher damping ratio compared to intact glass. For a simply supported rectangular pane, f1 ∝ (thickness / area²) × sqrt(elastic modulus/density). A hairline crack reduces effective stiffness locally, dropping f1 by 10-30% and increasing the -3 dB bandwidth of the resonance by 2-5×.
openings.verifier: Ground truth: visual inspection with polarized light or dye penetrant to confirm crack presence/length. Check: record 2 s of response to a finger tap, fit a damped sinusoid to extract f1 and damping ratio, compare to a reference database of intact panes of same dimensions.
openings.constructive_use: Quick safety check of glass facades, storefronts, or shower doors by a building manager using a phone app — no need to access both sides or use expensive ultrasonic glass testers.
openings.neglect_reason: Glass resonance monitoring is done in labs with impedance heads or laser vibrometers; no one has used a phone mic to extract damping ratio from a tap response and correlated it with crack length.
openings.alien_example: A hotel maintenance worker taps a window; the phone says 'Damping elevated — microcrack suspected. Recommend replacement.'

openings.domain: Rail / track vibration — loose spike detection
openings.signal: Impact-induced vibration from a hammer tap or passing wheel (100-1000 Hz)
openings.sensor: Smartphone accelerometer (or MEMS microphone) placed on the rail web
openings.coupling: A loose or missing rail spike (dogspike) reduces the vertical stiffness of the rail-foot connection. This increases the amplitude of the 2nd bending mode (around 400-600 Hz) relative to the 1st mode (100-200 Hz) because the loose spike changes boundary condition from clamped to simply supported. The ratio of mode 2 to mode 1 amplitude increases by >3 dB for a missing spike.
openings.verifier: Ground truth: visual inspection of spike condition (tight, loose, missing). Check: tap rail with a hammer 1 m from sensor, record 1 s, compute spectrogram, extract mode ratio, compare to known-good section.
openings.constructive_use: Low-cost track inspection by railway maintenance crews — attach phone to rail, tap with hammer, read spike health instantly. No need for expensive track geometry cars.
openings.neglect_reason: Track monitoring uses strain gauges or ultrasonic rail flaw detection; nobody has characterized the mode ratio change from a loose spike using a phone accelerometer.
openings.alien_example: A track worker places a phone on the rail, taps with a wrench, and the app shows 'Spike 4: loose. Torque to 150 N·m.'

openings.domain: Wooden beam / timber decay detection
openings.signal: Acoustic emission (AE) from micro-cracking under load (50-500 kHz, but structure-borne downshift to 1-10 kHz)
openings.sensor: Contact microphone (piezo disc) or smartphone accelerometer pressed into a pre-drilled pilot hole
openings.coupling: Fungal decay or dry rot in timber reduces the wood's modulus of rupture (MOR) and increases the rate of acoustic emission events under constant load. Healthy wood emits <5 AE events/min at 20% of failure load; decayed wood emits >50 events/min with a characteristic frequency peak at 3-5 kHz (cell wall fracture). The cumulative AE count correlates linearly with remaining strength.
openings.verifier: Ground truth: drill a small core sample, measure density and moisture content, perform a bending test on a matched sample. Check: apply a known load (e.g., 50 kg weight), record 5 min of contact audio, count threshold-crossing events >0.1 V, compare to calibration curve.
openings.constructive_use: Non-destructive assessment of historic timber beams, roof trusses, or railway sleepers — no need to cut or extract large samples. Use a phone and a piezo disc.
openings.neglect_reason: AE monitoring of timber is done with expensive resonant sensors (150 kHz) and multi-channel systems; nobody has used a $2 piezo disc in the audio range to count AE events from decay.
openings.alien_example: A conservation architect presses a sensor into a beam; the phone shows 'AE rate: 42 events/min — moderate decay. Remaining strength: ~60%.'

openings.domain: Machinery / bearing looseness detection
openings.signal: Vibration envelope of rotating machinery (10-1000 Hz, with modulation at shaft speed)
openings.sensor: Smartphone accelerometer (or MEMS gyroscope) magnetically attached to the machine housing
openings.coupling: A loose bearing in its housing (e.g., an electric motor fan bearing) produces a characteristic 'rattle' that modulates the vibration envelope at the shaft rotational frequency. The envelope spectrum shows sidebands around the bearing defect frequencies (ball-pass, cage) spaced at exactly 1× RPM. The ratio of sideband amplitude to carrier amplitude increases with clearance: a 0.1 mm radial clearance gives a sideband ratio of 0.3; 0.5 mm gives 0.8.
openings.verifier: Ground truth: measure bearing clearance with a dial indicator or feeler gauge after disassembly. Check: record 30 s of vibration at steady RPM, compute envelope spectrum via Hilbert transform, extract sideband-to-carrier ratio, compare to known-clearance samples.
openings.constructive_use: Predictive maintenance of industrial fans, pumps, and motors — a technician attaches a phone with a magnet sticker, runs an app, and gets bearing looseness severity without a $2000 vibration analyzer.
openings.neglect_reason: Bearing diagnostics use accelerometers with IEPE conditioning and FFT analyzers; nobody has shown that a phone accelerometer's noise floor is low enough to resolve envelope sidebands from a loose bearing, nor calibrated the sideband ratio vs. clearance.
openings.alien_example: A factory maintenance tech sticks a phone to a motor; the app shows 'Sideband ratio: 0.65 — bearing clearance ~0.4 mm. Schedule replacement within 2 weeks.'

openings.domain: traffic signal control for mixed-autonomy intersections
openings.strategy_space: phase-splitting policies that dynamically allocate green time fractions based on real-time lane occupancy and predicted arrival patterns from connected vehicles (0-50% penetration)
openings.simulator: SUMO (Simulation of Urban Mobility) with TraCI interface; score a policy by running 10-minute simulation of a 4x4 grid under random demand, measuring average vehicle delay and queue length
openings.value_if_found: reducing delay by 15-25% compared to actuated control, especially under fluctuating demand and low CV penetration
openings.neglect_reason: most RL traffic signal research uses full-observability or high CV penetration; low-penetration mixed-autonomy policies with partial observability are underexplored
openings.alien_example: a policy that only uses CV data from the upstream link to predict platoon arrival, then uses a phase-skip heuristic that skips the next phase if predicted arrivals are below a learned threshold

openings.domain: adaptive routing for urban delivery fleets with real-time traffic
openings.strategy_space: online route-selection heuristics that combine shortest-path with congestion-avoidance using live probe data and historical pattern matching
openings.simulator: SUMO with a custom delivery fleet plugin; score a heuristic by running 30-minute simulations on a 10x10 grid with 50 delivery requests, measuring total travel time and delivery completion rate
openings.value_if_found: 10-20% reduction in fleet-wide delivery time compared to dynamic shortest-path baselines
openings.neglect_reason: most routing research focuses on static or fully stochastic models; online heuristic spaces for mixed urban traffic with real-time feedback are under-explored
openings.alien_example: a 'greedy with lookahead' that reroutes only the most delayed vehicle in the fleet, using a learned delay predictor from local traffic data

openings.domain: congestion pricing for urban highway networks
openings.strategy_space: dynamic toll-setting policies that adjust per-lane tolls in real-time based on occupancy and speed thresholds, with hysteresis to prevent oscillation
openings.simulator: SUMO with a tolling plugin on a 5-link highway corridor; score a policy by running 1-hour simulation with realistic demand patterns, measuring total throughput and average travel time
openings.value_if_found: 5-12% throughput improvement or 10-20% travel time reduction compared to static tolls
openings.neglect_reason: most congestion pricing research uses static or time-of-day tolls; real-time adaptive policies with simple heuristics are rarely studied in simulation
openings.alien_example: a 'sticky threshold' policy: raise toll by 10% when speed drops below 40mph for 2 consecutive minutes, but only lower toll after speed exceeds 50mph for 5 minutes

openings.domain: bus priority at traffic signals in mixed-traffic corridors
openings.strategy_space: priority-request scheduling strategies that decide whether to extend green, truncate red, or skip a phase for a detected bus, balancing bus delay vs. cross-street traffic impact
openings.simulator: SUMO with a bus route plugin on a 10-intersection corridor; score a strategy by running 20-minute simulations with bus headways of 5-15 minutes, measuring bus delay and general traffic delay
openings.value_if_found: 20-40% reduction in bus delay with <5% increase in general traffic delay compared to no-priority or simple extend-only
openings.neglect_reason: most transit signal priority uses fixed rules; adaptive strategies that learn from real-time conditions (e.g., bus load, schedule adherence) are underexplored
openings.alien_example: a 'schedule-aware' strategy that only grants priority if the bus is more than 2 minutes behind schedule, using a learned delay threshold

openings.domain: pedestrian crossing timing at isolated intersections
openings.strategy_space: pedestrian call-response policies that decide whether to extend the walk phase or trigger a flashing don't walk based on pedestrian arrival rate and vehicle queue length
openings.simulator: SUMO with pedestrian plugin on a single 4-leg intersection; score a policy by running 1-hour simulation with random pedestrian arrivals (Poisson), measuring average pedestrian wait and vehicle delay
openings.value_if_found: 20-30% reduction in pedestrian wait time with <3% increase in vehicle delay compared to fixed-timing or actuated pedestrian control
openings.neglect_reason: pedestrian signal timing research is dominated by fixed or simple actuated control; adaptive heuristics that learn from real-time pedestrian counts are rare
openings.alien_example: a 'batch' policy: accumulate pedestrian calls for up to 10 seconds, then serve them all at once only if vehicle queue is below a learned threshold

openings.domain: emergency vehicle preemption in signal networks
openings.strategy_space: preemption-request prioritization policies that decide which emergency vehicle to serve first and how to clear the route (green wave vs. immediate all-red), considering multiple concurrent calls
openings.simulator: SUMO with emergency vehicle plugin on a 4x4 grid; score a policy by running 100 random emergency call scenarios, measuring response time and disruption to normal traffic (queue buildup)
openings.value_if_found: 15-25% reduction in emergency response time with <10% increase in background traffic delay compared to simple preemption
openings.neglect_reason: most emergency preemption uses simple all-red or green-wave; multi-vehicle coordination with learned heuristics is neglected
openings.alien_example: a 'queue-aware' preemption: if the emergency vehicle's route crosses a heavily queued intersection, pre-clear the queue by extending the green on the crossing street 30 seconds before arrival

openings.domain: network-wide signal timing coordination for grid networks
openings.strategy_space: offset and cycle-length assignment policies for a grid of intersections, using only local occupancy data and neighbor communication, without centralized optimization
openings.simulator: SUMO on a 6x6 grid with periodic demand patterns; score a policy by running 30-minute simulation with 10 random demand seeds, measuring average network delay and number of stops
openings.value_if_found: 10-20% reduction in network delay compared to isolated actuated control or simple coordinated fixed-timing
openings.neglect_reason: most coordinated signal timing uses centralized optimization (e.g., TRANSYT) or fully distributed RL; simple decentralized heuristics using only neighbor info are underexplored
openings.alien_example: a 'consensus' policy: each intersection adjusts its offset toward the average of its neighbors' offsets, weighted by link congestion, updated every 2 cycles

openings.domain: ramp metering for highway on-ramps with real-time mainline traffic
openings.strategy_space: metering rate policies that adjust per-lane release rates based on mainline speed, occupancy, and downstream queue spillback risk
openings.simulator: SUMO on a 10km highway with 5 on-ramps and 3 off-ramps; score a policy by running 1-hour simulation with realistic demand, measuring mainline throughput and average speed
openings.value_if_found: 5-15% increase in mainline throughput or 10-20% reduction in travel time compared to fixed-time or ALINEA-like metering
openings.neglect_reason: most ramp metering research uses ALINEA or simple occupancy-based; adaptive policies that consider downstream congestion and queue spillback are underexplored
openings.alien_example: a 'downstream-aware' policy: if the downstream segment occupancy exceeds 70%, reduce metering rate by 20% to prevent queue spillback onto the ramp

openings.domain: PCB component placement for thermal balancing
openings.objective: minimize_max_temperature: given a set of heat-generating components (ICs, regulators) and a board outline with pre-placed connectors, score a placement by computing steady-state temperature map via simplified thermal resistance network (cheap iterative solver)
openings.space: 10-50 components, each with 5-20 possible orientations and positions on a ~100x100 grid; ~10^100 placements
openings.value_if_solved: reduces hot spots by 15-30% without expensive CFD simulation; enables smaller heatsinks/fans in consumer electronics
openings.neglect_reason: PCB EDA tools (Altium, KiCad) only offer manual thermal hints; automated placement optimizers ignore thermal coupling between components
openings.alien_example: components placed in spiral patterns radiating from hot zones, or tall components arranged as 'wind tunnels' despite being in still air

openings.domain: VLSI standard-cell placement with wirelength + density gradient
openings.objective: minimize_HPWL_plus_density_variance: half-perimeter wirelength + penalty for cell density >0.7 per grid bin (10x10 bins), computed via sorted coordinates and bin counting
openings.space: 1000-10000 cells on a 2D grid; ~10^10000 placements
openings.value_if_solved: produces legalizable placements 2-5x faster than academic placers (ePlace, NTUplace) for small-to-medium blocks
openings.neglect_reason: modern VLSI placers use complex analytical gradients; no one explores simple combinatorial heuristics on this specific cheap objective
openings.alien_example: cells arranged in concentric rings around the most-connected cell, or in diagonal stripes to reduce congestion

openings.domain: PCB trace routing for crosstalk avoidance (2-layer board)
openings.objective: minimize_peak_crosstalk: given fixed component pads and netlist, score a routing (via Steiner trees on grid) by computing worst-case coupling capacitance between parallel segments >1mm, using closed-form microstrip formulas
openings.space: 10-30 nets, each with 2-10 terminals on a ~50x50 grid; ~10^50 routings
openings.value_if_solved: reduces signal integrity issues in mixed-signal PCBs without full EM simulation; cuts design iterations by 30%
openings.neglect_reason: PCB autorouters (Freerouting, TopoR) ignore crosstalk; SI tools (HyperLynx) are post-route verification only
openings.alien_example: routes that deliberately meander to spread parallel runs across different layers, or use 'zigzag' patterns to break coupling length

openings.domain: FPGA logic block packing for routability
openings.objective: minimize_congestion_penalty: given a netlist of LUTs and FFs, pack them into CLBs (each holds 4 LUTs+8 FFs), score by counting routing tracks needed per routing channel (Chebyshev distance between CLBs) vs. channel capacity
openings.space: 100-1000 logic elements into 25-250 CLBs; ~10^200 packings
openings.value_if_solved: reduces routability-driven placement iterations by 20% for mid-size FPGA designs (Xilinx 7-series)
openings.neglect_reason: Vivado uses greedy packing; academic packers (T-VPACK) optimize only for delay, not routability
openings.alien_example: packings that cluster high-fanout nets into neighboring CLBs, or leave 'holes' for routing channels

openings.domain: Warehouse bin packing for mixed pallet loading with stability
openings.objective: maximize_volume_utilization_minus_tilt_penalty: given boxes of 3-5 sizes and a pallet with max height, score a layer-by-layer arrangement by computing filled volume + penalty for boxes with >50% overhang (unstable)
openings.space: 30-80 boxes per pallet, each placed on a 10x10 grid; ~10^60 arrangements
openings.value_if_solved: reduces shipping costs by 5-10% in e-commerce warehouses that currently use manual stacking or simple greedy algorithms
openings.neglect_reason: palletizing software (TOPS, CAPE) focuses on column-stacking; no cheap stability metric is used in optimization
openings.alien_example: arrangements where boxes form interlocking 'brick wall' patterns, or where heavy boxes are placed at edges for counterbalance

openings.domain: Hospital nurse shift scheduling with preference equity
openings.objective: minimize_max_regret: given 10-30 nurses with shift preferences (1-5), 7-day schedule, score by computing for each nurse the sum of squared deviations from their preferred shift count, then take the maximum across nurses
openings.space: 30 nurses x 7 days x 3 shifts = 630 binary variables; ~10^189 assignments
openings.value_if_solved: reduces nurse dissatisfaction turnover by 15% in mid-size hospital units
openings.neglect_reason: nurse scheduling literature uses MILP with complex constraints; no one optimizes this specific max-regret objective with simple heuristics
openings.alien_example: schedules where nurses with similar preferences are paired on opposite shifts, or where unpopular shifts are clustered to minimize total regret

openings.domain: Drone delivery route planning with battery swap stations
openings.objective: minimize_total_delivery_time: given 10-50 delivery points and 3-5 swap stations on a grid, score a route (sequence of deliveries + potential station visits) by computing Manhattan distance segments, with 5 min penalty per swap
openings.space: 20-50 stops, each with 2-3 choices of which station to use; ~10^40 routes
openings.value_if_solved: enables 20% more deliveries per battery in urban drone logistics (Wing, Zipline)
openings.neglect_reason: drone routing papers focus on energy-aware TSP; no one combines cheap Manhattan distance with station choice in this specific form
openings.alien_example: routes that visit stations just before long deliveries, or that cluster deliveries around a single station then jump to another cluster

openings.domain: 2D irregular shape nesting for leather cutting
openings.objective: minimize_waste_area: given 10-30 irregular polygonal parts (shoe patterns) and a rectangular hide with defects, score a placement by computing total area of bounding box minus sum of part areas, with penalty for parts over defect regions
openings.space: 10-30 parts, each with 36 rotations and 100x100 position grid; ~10^200 placements
openings.value_if_solved: reduces leather waste by 5-10% in footwear manufacturing (currently 15-20% waste)
openings.neglect_reason: nesting software (Optitex, Lectra) uses expensive no-fit polygon computation; no one tries cheap bounding-box approximation with defect penalty
openings.alien_example: parts arranged in interlocking 'puzzle' patterns that fill concave regions of other parts, or rotated to align straight edges with defect boundaries

openings.domain: Bistable acoustic switches for noise-control labyrinths
openings.verifier: k-Wave: simulate nonlinear pressure-dependent transmission through bistable membrane/channel geometries; score by dB attenuation difference between stable states
openings.search_space: Membrane thickness, prestress, cavity depth, neck geometry — all continuous; ~10^6 combinations per topology
openings.neglect_reason: Bistable acoustics studied only in 1D lumped models; full 2D/3D geometry search never attempted
openings.alien_example: A clover-shaped cavity with 3 stable membrane positions that switch transmission from -2 dB to -25 dB at 500 Hz

openings.domain: Graded-index acoustic lenses from random foam-like pore distributions
openings.verifier: k-Wave: 2D/3D simulation of pressure propagation through pixelated porosity maps; score by focal spot size and intensity relative to diffraction limit
openings.search_space: Binary porosity pattern (10×10 to 50×50 grid) — 2^(2500) possibilities per lens
openings.neglect_reason: Current graded-index lenses use regular lattices or hand-designed gradients; stochastic porous lenses are unexplored
openings.alien_example: A 30×30 binary pattern that focuses 10 kHz ultrasound to a spot 0.3λ wide, shaped like a fractal tree

openings.domain: Acoustic diffusers with non-Euclidean surface tessellations
openings.verifier: k-Wave: simulate reflection from 2D surface profiles; score by diffusion coefficient (uniformity of scattered polar pattern) at 1-4 kHz
openings.search_space: Penrose tiling, hyperbolic tilings, or Voronoi cell heights — continuous height per cell × combinatorial tiling choice; ~10^20+
openings.neglect_reason: All commercial diffusers use Schroeder sequences or primitive binary arrays; non-periodic tilings never tested
openings.alien_example: A hyperbolic {7,3} tiling with heights following a prime-number sequence that scatters sound evenly over 180° at 2 kHz

openings.domain: Acoustic vortex generators with chiral lattice cores
openings.verifier: k-Wave: simulate phase and amplitude of transmitted field through 3D chiral lattice; score by orbital angular momentum purity (modal decomposition)
openings.search_space: Chirality angle, strut thickness, lattice periodicity, number of unit cells — 6 continuous parameters × 3 symmetry families
openings.neglect_reason: Acoustic vortices generated only with phased arrays or spiral gratings; volumetric chiral lattices never explored
openings.alien_example: A 4×4×4 tetrachiral lattice that converts plane wave to pure l=3 vortex at 5 kHz with 90% efficiency

openings.domain: Acoustic rainbow-trapping structures with tapered coupled resonators
openings.verifier: k-Wave: 1D/2D frequency sweep through tapered waveguide with side-branch resonators; score by broadband slow-sound bandwidth and group index
openings.search_space: Taper function (polynomial, exponential, sinusoidal) × resonator spacing law × resonator geometry (neck width, cavity volume) — ~10^12 continuous combos
openings.neglect_reason: Rainbow trapping demonstrated only with straight waveguides and uniform resonators; taper+resonator co-optimization is untouched

openings.domain: Acoustic cloaking shells with aperiodic layered media
openings.verifier: k-Wave: 2D simulation of plane wave scattering from cylinder with concentric shell layers; score by scattering cross-section reduction relative to bare cylinder
openings.search_space: Layer thicknesses (continuous, 5-20 layers) × material properties (density, speed of sound) — ~10^15 combos for 10 layers
openings.neglect_reason: All acoustic cloaks use periodic or monotonic gradient layers; aperiodic sequences (Fibonacci, Thue-Morse, random) never systematically searched

openings.domain: Acoustic non-reciprocal circulators using time-modulated Helmholtz resonators
openings.verifier: k-Wave: simulate 2D pressure field with time-varying cavity volumes (modulation function); score by isolation ratio (forward/backward transmission difference)

openings.neglect_reason: Non-reciprocal acoustics achieved with fans, nonlinearities, or complex active arrays; simple time-modulated passive resonators are virtually unstudied
openings.alien_example: A 3-port circulator using sinusoidal modulation at 0.5× carrier frequency, achieving 20 dB isolation with 3 passive cavities

openings.domain: vibration / structural health
openings.signal: Low-frequency ground vibrations from nearby traffic or machinery propagating through building foundations
openings.sensor: Phone accelerometer (placed on floor or window sill)
openings.coupling: Traffic or industrial vibrations couple into the building's structure, creating surface waves that modulate the phone's accelerometer readings at 1-50 Hz. The specific frequency content and amplitude encode the type and proximity of the vibration source.
openings.verifier: Place a second accelerometer (e.g., ADXL335, $5) at the same location and compare time-frequency spectrograms. Cross-correlation of peaks confirms the phone's signal matches the reference.
openings.constructive_use: Map structural resonance modes and soil-structure interaction of a building over time without installing permanent sensors; detect early signs of foundation settlement or loosening joints.
openings.neglect_reason: Phone accelerometers are ubiquitous but almost never used for long-term structural health monitoring because they are considered too noisy and low-resolution. The coupling via ground is ignored in favor of expensive geophones.
openings.alien_example: A building 'listens' to the footsteps of its own occupants to learn which floors have loose tiles, by treating footstep vibrations as a diagnostic probe.

openings.domain: Adaptive traffic signal control for mixed-autonomy intersections
openings.strategy_space: Signal phase timing policies (phase order, duration, offsets) for 4-approach intersection with varying fractions of connected/autonomous vehicles (CAVs) and human-driven vehicles
openings.simulator: SUMO (Simulation of Urban MObility) with TraCI interface: test a candidate policy by running 10-minute rush-hour simulation on a single intersection, measuring average wait time and throughput (<60 seconds on laptop)
openings.value_if_found: 5-15% reduction in average delay vs. actuated or fixed-time control, especially in mixed-autonomy regimes where CAV penetration is 20-60%
openings.neglect_reason: Most signal control research focuses on full-human or full-autonomy; mixed-autonomy regimes are underexplored due to complexity of modeling human-CAV interactions

openings.domain: Congestion-aware dynamic tolling for urban perimeter control
openings.strategy_space: Toll values (0-10$) per entry point to an urban cordon zone, updated every 5 minutes based on instantaneous occupancy and queue lengths

openings.value_if_found: 10-20% reduction in total vehicle-hours traveled compared to fixed toll or simple occupancy-based tolling
openings.neglect_reason: Perimeter control literature focuses on gating (metering) rather than pricing; toll-based perimeter control remains mostly theoretical with simple threshold rules
openings.alien_example: Toll policy that lowers price when occupancy is moderate (to encourage spreading) and spikes only when occupancy exceeds 85%, creating a 'smoothing' effect rather than hard cap

openings.domain: Bus bunching mitigation via stop-skipping and holding heuristics
openings.strategy_space: Decision rules for each bus at each stop: hold (0-120 seconds) or skip stop, based on headway to preceding bus, passenger count, and time since last stop
openings.simulator: Discrete-event bus route simulator (e.g., BusMezzo or custom Python sim) with 10 buses on 20-stop circular route, scoring by total passenger wait time + variance in headways (<30 seconds per candidate)
openings.value_if_found: 20-30% reduction in average passenger wait time compared to schedule-based holding or no control
openings.neglect_reason: Existing bus control uses simple threshold rules (hold if headway < threshold); continuous policy spaces with learned heuristics are rarely explored

openings.domain: Packet routing in delay-tolerant networks with intermittent connectivity
openings.strategy_space: Forwarding heuristics: which encountered node to forward a packet to, based on node contact history, battery level, and destination proximity (binary decisions per contact event)
openings.simulator: ns-3 with DTN module: simulate 50 mobile nodes in 1km^2 area for 1 hour, scoring by delivery ratio and latency (<5 minutes for 10 random seeds)
openings.value_if_found: 15-25% improvement in delivery ratio vs. epidemic routing or Spray-and-Wait, especially under sparse/partitioned conditions
openings.neglect_reason: Most DTN routing uses hand-designed heuristics (PROPHET, MaxProp); learned policies from contact traces are rare due to sparse reward signals

openings.domain: Continuous double auction strategy for limit order book market making
openings.strategy_space: Quoting policy: bid-ask spread, quote sizes, and cancellation timing as functions of order book imbalance, volatility, and inventory
openings.simulator: ABIDES (Agent-Based Interactive Discrete Event Simulator) for a single stock with 1000 simulated traders: evaluate a market-making strategy over 1 hour of simulated time (runs in ~3 minutes on laptop)
openings.value_if_found: Higher Sharpe ratio and lower adverse selection than standard Avellaneda-Stoikov or naive spread strategies, especially in low-liquidity regimes
