openings.domain: Water reservoir release policies for flood mitigation and hydropower
openings.strategy_space: Release rate (m^3/s) as function of current reservoir level, inflow forecast (24h), and downstream river stage, with daily decisions
openings.simulator: Simple reservoir-routing model (e.g., HEC-ResSim or custom Python lumped model) for a single reservoir with 5 years of historical inflow data: score by flood damage avoided + hydropower revenue (<1 minute per candidate)
openings.value_if_found: 10-15% improvement in combined objective vs. standard rule curves or PID-based release, especially under non-stationary inflow patterns
openings.neglect_reason: Reservoir operations are dominated by fixed rule curves or model predictive control; learned heuristic policies are rare due to regulatory conservatism
openings.alien_example: Policy that intentionally pre-releases water when reservoir is 60% full and 3-day forecast shows >80th percentile inflow, even if downstream river is moderate, to create flood storage

openings.domain: Evolutionary metaheuristic for job shop scheduling with machine breakdowns
openings.strategy_space: Dispatching rules (e.g., SPT, EDD, CR, FIFO) and their parameters for each machine, plus how to switch rules when breakdowns occur
openings.simulator: Discrete-event job shop simulator (e.g., OR-Tools or custom Python) with 10 machines, 100 jobs, 5% breakdown probability: score by makespan and tardiness (<10 seconds per candidate)
openings.value_if_found: 5-10% better makespan and 15-20% lower tardiness than best single dispatching rule, especially under dynamic breakdown patterns
openings.neglect_reason: Job shop scheduling focuses on static optimization or single dispatching rules; adaptive rule-switching policies are rarely systematically searched
openings.alien_example: Rule that switches from SPT to CR when machine queue length exceeds 10 and 3+ jobs are already late, then reverts to SPT when queue clears

openings.domain: Adaptive cruise control (ACC) gap selection for fuel efficiency in mixed traffic
openings.strategy_space: Time-gap setting (0.5-3.0 seconds) as function of preceding vehicle speed, road grade, and surrounding vehicle types (human vs. automated)
openings.simulator: SUMO with electric vehicle energy model (or simple physics-based fuel model): simulate 10 platooning vehicles over 5km highway with varying grades, scoring by total energy consumption (<1 minute per candidate)
openings.value_if_found: 8-12% energy reduction compared to fixed 1.5s gap, especially in stop-and-go traffic with 30-50% CAV penetration
openings.neglect_reason: ACC gap research focuses on constant or speed-dependent gaps; learned policies that account for surrounding vehicle automation level are unexplored
openings.alien_example: Policy that uses 0.8s gap when following another ACC vehicle but 2.0s gap when following a human driver, and dynamically adjusts based on human driver's jerk variance

openings.domain: PCB component placement for thermal management
openings.objective: minimize peak temperature and thermal gradient given component power dissipation and board geometry, computed by fast thermal simulation (e.g., compact RC network or steady-state finite-difference solver)
openings.space: 10^100+ (typical PCB has 50-500 components, each with many rotation/flip variants, plus layer allocation)
openings.value_if_solved: Reduced thermal failures, fewer heatsinks/fans, higher power density in compact electronics (e.g., LED drivers, power supplies, automotive ECUs)
openings.neglect_reason: Most EDA tools treat placement as purely electrical/routing-driven; thermal is checked late via slow CFD. No cheap objective exists in standard optimization loops.
openings.alien_example: Place a 1.5W regulator directly under a tall electrolytic capacitor to use its body as a passive heat spreader, while rotating a 0.8W FET 45° to align its copper pad with a board via array

openings.domain: VLSI standard-cell placement for clock-tree-friendly wirelength
openings.objective: minimize sum of half-perimeter wirelength weighted by clock skew sensitivity of each net, computed by fast HPWL metric on placed cells (no routing needed)
openings.space: 10^10000+ (millions of cells in modern chips, each has ~10 possible sites per row)
openings.value_if_solved: 10-20% reduction in clock power and timing closure iterations, directly lowering chip cost and time-to-market for ASICs and SoCs
openings.neglect_reason: Academic placement benchmarks optimize pure wirelength; industry uses proprietary clock-tree synthesis after placement. No open benchmark for skew-aware placement exists.
openings.alien_example: Cluster all flip-flops fed by the same clock buffer into a compact diamond shape, while pushing a long combinational chain into a winding path that balances load capacitance per clock phase

openings.domain: Restaurant meal-prep scheduling with limited kitchen equipment
openings.objective: minimize total makespan and ingredient waste, computed by discrete-event simulation of cooking times, oven/range/stove occupancy, and ingredient shelf-life decay
openings.space: 10^50+ (50-200 menu items per shift, each with 3-15 sequential steps, shared equipment constraints)
openings.value_if_solved: 30-50% reduction in food waste, faster table turns, lower labor cost for casual dining and fast-casual chains (e.g., 50-location regional chain)
openings.neglect_reason: Kitchen scheduling is done by human intuition or simple FIFO; academic job-shop scheduling ignores perishable ingredients and multi-step recipes with parallel cooking.
openings.alien_example: Start searing the steak 4 minutes before the pasta water boils, then use the now-free grill to toast buns while the sauce reduces—saving 90 seconds on the burger station

openings.domain: PCB routing order optimization for crosstalk reduction
openings.objective: minimize total crosstalk energy on victim nets given signal edge rates and coupling lengths, computed by fast analytical coupling model (closed-form mutual capacitance/integration along parallel runs)
openings.space: 10^30+ (100-1000 nets, each can be routed in 2-10 different orders/layers, plus differential pair twisting variants)
openings.value_if_solved: Fewer signal integrity failures in high-speed digital (e.g., DDR5, PCIe5), reducing board spins from 3 to 1, saving $50k+ per design
openings.neglect_reason: PCB autorouters route nets sequentially by length or net class; no commercial tool optimizes routing order for crosstalk. Academic work focuses on post-layout fixing.
openings.alien_example: Route the 8-bit data bus in order D7→D0 (bit-reversed) so that the most critical DQS strobe runs perpendicular to the noisiest D7, then snake D3 around a via to break a 300mil parallel run

openings.domain: Warehouse bin-packing of irregularly shaped e-commerce items
openings.objective: maximize volumetric utilization of shipping totes given 3D item geometry (point cloud or voxel representation), computed by fast greedy fill rate (no physics simulation)
openings.space: 10^100+ (50-200 items per order, each with 6 rotation axes and arbitrary shape, ~20 tote sizes)
openings.value_if_solved: 15-25% reduction in shipping costs and cardboard waste for large e-commerce fulfillment centers (e.g., 1M+ orders/day)
openings.neglect_reason: Bin-packing literature focuses on rectangles or cylinders; real items are irregular (plush toys, tools with handles, bundled cables). No cheap objective exists for arbitrary 3D shapes.
openings.alien_example: Nest a coffee mug upside-down over a bottle of vitamins, then slide a flexible mouse pad along the curved gap—achieving 92% fill vs 68% with naive stacking

openings.domain: Hospital nurse shift scheduling with fatigue dynamics
openings.objective: minimize predicted fatigue accumulation (weighted sum of consecutive shifts, night shifts, and recovery gaps) computed by a simple linear fatigue model (no physiological simulation)
openings.space: 10^80+ (20-100 nurses, 7-28 day horizon, 3-5 shift types, each with 5-15 constraint types)
openings.value_if_solved: Reduced medical errors and burnout; 10-20% lower turnover in nursing staff for a 300-bed hospital
openings.neglect_reason: Nurse scheduling tools use hard constraints (max shifts, min rest) but ignore cumulative fatigue dynamics. Academic models are too complex for daily use.
openings.alien_example: Assign Nurse A to 3 day shifts, then a night shift, then 2 days off—not the standard 5 days on—because her fatigue model shows she recovers faster with a split break

openings.domain: PCB via placement optimization for return-path continuity
openings.objective: minimize total loop inductance of critical high-speed signals by placing stitching vias near signal via transitions, computed by fast partial-inductance formula (no full-wave EM)
openings.space: 10^40+ (50-500 critical nets, each with 2-10 via transitions, hundreds of possible stitch-via locations per transition)
openings.value_if_solved: Lower EMI emissions and improved signal integrity in multi-layer PCBs (e.g., 10-layer server boards), reducing design iterations by 1-2 spins
openings.neglect_reason: PCB layout engineers place stitching vias manually or with simple rules (e.g., one per transition). No tool optimizes via cluster geometry for minimum inductance.
openings.alien_example: Place 3 stitching vias in a tight triangle around a differential pair via, but offset them 15° to avoid creating a resonant cavity with the power plane cutout

openings.domain: Last-mile delivery route planning with dynamic parking constraints
openings.objective: minimize total walking distance from parking spots to delivery points, given real-time parking availability probabilities, computed by simple Euclidean distance aggregation (no traffic simulation)
openings.space: 10^60+ (50-200 stops per route, 2-5 parking zones per stop, time-dependent parking probability)
openings.value_if_solved: 15-30% reduction in delivery time and fuel cost for urban package delivery fleets (e.g., Amazon, UPS in dense cities)
openings.neglect_reason: Routing algorithms assume parking at each stop; real drivers circle blocks. No cheap objective incorporates probabilistic parking availability.
openings.alien_example: Route the driver to park 80m away at a loading zone with 90% availability, instead of double-parking directly in front (20% chance of a ticket), then deliver 3 packages on a 120m walking loop

openings.domain: Low-Profile Metasurface Antennas for Non-Standard Impedance Loads
openings.verifier: openEMS: FDTD simulation of S11, gain, and pattern; score = fitness to target impedance over 1–10 GHz
openings.search_space: 10–200 unit cells (patch + via + slot shapes), each parameterised by 4–8 continuous dimensions (edge lengths, dielectric constant, substrate height), ~10^40 combos
openings.neglect_reason: Mainstream antenna design focuses on 50Ω ports; non-50Ω loads (e.g., rectennas, high-impedance mixers) are niche, yet metasurfaces can impedance-transform without extra matching networks. Big labs chase 5G/6G arrays, not this corner.
openings.alien_example: A 3-layer metasurface with 7 irregularly shaped patches that, when fed by a 300Ω differential line, achieves >90% efficiency from 3.1–3.8 GHz with a radiation pattern shaped like a tilted cardioid — no one would draw that topology.

openings.domain: Passive RFID Tag Antennas for Arbitrary Object Shapes (Non-Planar)
openings.verifier: openEMS: simulate impedance matching + read range on a 3D mesh of the object (e.g., a bottle, a shoe) at 860–960 MHz
openings.search_space: Freeform 3D antenna traces on surface of object, parameterised as N control points (N=5–20) with 2D coordinates on the object mesh, plus trace width; ~10^30 designs
openings.neglect_reason: Commercial RFID tags are generic dipoles on flat labels; conformal antennas for specific products (wine bottles, medical vials) are custom-designed by hand. AI can exploit the object’s dielectric to tune impedance — unexplored systematically.
openings.alien_example: A helical-like trace that wraps around the neck of a wine bottle, with variable pitch and a stub that couples to the liquid, achieving 8m read range at 915 MHz — a human would just put a straight dipole on the side.

openings.domain: Electromagnetic Energy Harvesters with Non-Rectangular Coil Shapes
openings.verifier: openEMS or FEMM: simulate induced voltage from a time-varying magnetic field (e.g., 50 Hz power line) into arbitrary planar/spiral coil
openings.search_space: Coil defined by 10–50 control points in 2D, trace width, number of turns (discrete), layer stack; ~10^35 combos
openings.neglect_reason: Harvester coils are always square or circular spirals; non-convex, branched, or fractal shapes can capture flux more efficiently from near-field sources. Big research focuses on rectifier circuits, not coil geometry.
openings.alien_example: A coil that looks like a distorted snowflake with 6 lobes, each lobe having a different turn density, resonating at 50 Hz with 3x the open-circuit voltage of an equal-area square spiral — no one would draw that.

openings.domain: Dielectric Resonator Antennas (DRAs) with Arbitrary 3D Shapes
openings.verifier: openEMS or CST (if available): simulate S11, bandwidth, gain for a freeform DRA on a ground plane, 2–10 GHz
openings.search_space: 3D shape defined by 20–100 voxels or a signed-distance function with 8–16 parameters (e.g., superquadric + perturbations); ~10^50
openings.neglect_reason: DRAs are almost always rectangular, cylindrical, or hemispherical — simple analytic modes. Freeform shapes can support multiple modes, widen bandwidth, or shape pattern. Only a few papers explore genetic algorithms on simple parameter sets.
openings.alien_example: A DRA shaped like a twisted torus with a central hole and 4 protruding fins, operating at 5.8 GHz with 40% bandwidth and a null in the zenith direction — no textbook would predict that.

openings.domain: Frequency-Selective Surfaces (FSS) with Non-Periodic Aperiodic Unit Cells
openings.verifier: openEMS: simulate transmission/reflection through a finite array (10x10 to 30x30) of individually shaped cells
openings.search_space: Each unit cell is a freeform metallic patch (10–50 parameters), array layout is a set of 100–900 cells, each can differ; effectively ~10^1000
openings.neglect_reason: FSS design assumes periodic repetition of a single cell to get analytic response. Aperiodic FSS can create arbitrary spatial filters, beam-shaping, or cloaking, but is computationally heavy — exactly where cheap AI + simulator shine.
openings.alien_example: A 20x20 array where every cell is a different irregular spline shape, collectively producing a band-stop at 10 GHz with a spatial null on the right side — humans would never design each cell individually.

openings.domain: Near-Field Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) Coils with Non-Planar Topology
openings.verifier: openEMS or FEMM: simulate coupling coefficient k and efficiency between two arbitrary 3D coil shapes at 6.78 MHz
openings.search_space: Two coils, each defined by 10–30 control points in 3D (wire path), number of turns, wire gauge, ferrite backing shape; ~10^40
openings.neglect_reason: WPT coils are almost always planar spirals or solenoids. 3D non-coplanar coils (e.g., conical, twisted, branched) can improve misalignment tolerance or reduce leakage. Big labs focus on circuit-side optimization (resonance, impedance).
openings.alien_example: A transmitter coil shaped like a saddle (hyperbolic paraboloid) and a receiver coil like a helical cone, achieving 85% efficiency at 5 cm misalignment — no one would draw that pair.

openings.domain: Electromagnetic Cloaking Structures for Metallic Objects at Microwave Frequencies
openings.verifier: openEMS: simulate radar cross-section (RCS) reduction from 2–18 GHz for a freeform cloaking shell around a conducting sphere/cylinder
openings.search_space: Cloak shape is a 3D shell defined by 10–30 parameters (e.g., radial thickness profile, dielectric constant gradient, metallic patch pattern on surface); ~10^30
openings.neglect_reason: Most cloaking research uses analytic transformation optics (spherical/cylindrical symmetry) or bulky metamaterials. Freeform non-symmetric cloaks for arbitrary objects are rarely explored due to high simulation cost — AI can brute-force search.
openings.alien_example: A cloak that looks like a lumpy potato with a metallic patch grid on its surface, reducing RCS of a 2 cm steel sphere by 20 dB at 10 GHz — no human would guess that shape.

openings.domain: Microwave Filters with Non-Planar 3D Conductor Patterns (Additive Manufacturing)
openings.verifier: openEMS: simulate S-parameters (S11, S21) from 1–20 GHz for a freeform 3D metallic structure inside a waveguide or on a substrate
openings.search_space: 3D conductor path defined by 20–100 nodes in 3D space, variable cross-section (rectangular, circular), dielectric support shape; ~10^60
openings.neglect_reason: Conventional filters use planar microstrip, SIW, or cavity resonators with simple shapes (rectangles, circles). 3D-printed freeform filters can achieve unique coupling topologies, but design is still manual. Big RF houses use standard topologies.
openings.alien_example: A filter that looks like a tangled wire tree with 7 branches, each branch a different length, creating a bandpass at 8 GHz with 3 notches at 9, 11, 13 GHz — a human would use a coupled-line filter instead.

openings.domain: Dynamic traffic signal control at isolated intersections
openings.strategy_space: Phase timing policies (green split, cycle length, offset) for multiple traffic streams with varying arrival patterns
openings.simulator: SUMO (Simulation of Urban MObility) with TraCI interface: run a single intersection for 10 simulated minutes with random vehicle arrivals, measure average wait time per vehicle in seconds
openings.value_if_found: Reducing average delay by 15-30% compared to actuated control without requiring expensive hardware or centralized coordination
openings.neglect_reason: Most research focuses on coordinated networks or deep RL with high compute; simple adaptive heuristics for isolated intersections are underexplored
openings.alien_example: A policy that predicts next 3 vehicle platoons via a tiny LSTM and sets phase durations to minimize squared queue lengths, trained on 100 SUMO runs

openings.domain: Bufferbloat mitigation in home routers
openings.strategy_space: Active queue management (AQM) parameters: min/max thresholds, marking probability slope, EWMA weight for CoDel/PIE variants
openings.simulator: ns-3 with a simple dumbbell topology (1 bottleneck link, 10 TCP flows, 1 UDP flow); run for 30 seconds, measure 95th percentile latency and goodput
openings.value_if_found: Achieving <20ms latency under 100Mbps load while maintaining >90% link utilization, beating CoDel and fq_codel
openings.neglect_reason: AQM research is mature but mostly hand-tuned; automated discovery of new functional forms (not just parameter tuning) is rare
openings.alien_example: An AQM that uses a 2-tap digital filter on queue derivative to predict incipient congestion, with coefficients evolved via CMA-ES

openings.domain: Wireless mesh network channel allocation
openings.strategy_space: Assignment of 802.11 channels to mesh nodes (11 channels, 20 nodes) minimizing interference + maximizing throughput
openings.simulator: ns-3 with mesh module: create random 20-node topologies, run 60-second UDP CBR traffic, measure aggregate throughput in Mbps
openings.value_if_found: 20-40% throughput improvement over greedy/random allocation with same number of radios
openings.neglect_reason: Most work uses ILP or graph coloring; heuristic search for novel channel assignment policies (e.g., based on node degree + traffic load) is sparse
openings.alien_example: A channel assignment rule: assign channel = (node_id XOR floor(traffic_load*10)) mod 11, tested with Bayesian optimization over 3 parameters

openings.domain: TCP congestion control for satellite links
openings.strategy_space: Congestion window update rules (AIAD, AIMD, MIMD variants with different alpha/beta/gamma schedules) for high-BDP, high-loss links
openings.simulator: ns-3 with satellite channel model (250ms RTT, 1% random loss, 50Mbps): run single flow for 60 seconds, measure average throughput and Jain fairness index
openings.value_if_found: Doubling throughput vs. Cubic while maintaining fairness, without needing explicit feedback
openings.neglect_reason: TCP variants are mostly designed for terrestrial links; satellite-specific heuristics beyond Hybla and TCP-Peach are rare
openings.alien_example: A control law: cwnd = cwnd * (1 + (RTT_min/RTT)^2 - loss_rate) per RTT, discovered by genetic programming

openings.domain: Packet scheduling in software-defined networks
openings.strategy_space: Priority assignment rules for flows based on header fields (port, IP, protocol, packet size, flow duration) to minimize tail latency
openings.simulator: Mininet with custom switch: replay a 1000-flow data center trace (from public CAIDA dataset), measure FCT (flow completion time) 99th percentile
openings.value_if_found: Reducing tail FCT by 50% compared to FIFO with minimal overhead (no per-flow state)
openings.neglect_reason: Most SDN scheduling uses heavyweight ML or fixed priorities; simple hash-based heuristics that adapt to traffic patterns are underexplored
openings.alien_example: A priority = (source_port mod 4) + (packet_size < 500 ? 2 : 0) + (protocol==UDP ? 1 : 0), evolved via tournament selection over 100 simulator runs

openings.domain: Congestion-aware routing in low-power IoT networks (RPL)
openings.strategy_space: Objective function parameters for RPL: how to combine ETX, hop count, queue length, energy into a rank metric
openings.simulator: Cooja (Contiki OS simulator): 50-node random topology, UDP traffic to sink, run 10 minutes, measure PDR (packet delivery ratio) and average latency
openings.value_if_found: Achieving >95% PDR under high traffic (10 packets/min per node) vs. 70-80% for MRHOF
openings.neglect_reason: RPL standards define few objective functions; custom parameterizations or new metric formulas are rarely systematically searched
openings.alien_example: A rank = ETX * (1 + queue_length/10) - 0.5*(RSSI/100), discovered by random mutation hill climbing

openings.domain: Load balancing in multipath TCP (MPTCP)
openings.strategy_space: Subflow selection heuristics: which network interface to use for each new packet based on RTT, bandwidth, loss, battery
openings.simulator: ns-3 with MPTCP module: 2 paths (WiFi + cellular), 30-second file transfer, measure throughput and energy consumption (Joules per MB)
openings.value_if_found: Achieving 90% of optimal throughput while using 40% less energy vs. default minRTT scheduler
openings.neglect_reason: MPTCP schedulers are mostly hand-designed (minRTT, redundant, BLEST); automated discovery of hybrid policies is rare
openings.alien_example: A scheduler: if WiFi_RTT < 2*cellular_RTT and WiFi_bandwidth > 5Mbps, use WiFi; else send 70% on cellular, evolved via particle swarm optimization

openings.domain: Congestion control for QUIC over high-latency links
openings.strategy_space: QUIC's pacing rate and loss detection thresholds (e.g., time threshold vs. packet threshold, initial window, minimum RTO)
openings.simulator: ns-3 with QUIC module (quic-ns-3 fork): 200ms RTT, 10% reordering, 30-second connection, measure throughput and retransmission rate
openings.value_if_found: Maintaining 80% link utilization while reducing spurious retransmits by 60% compared to NewReno
openings.neglect_reason: QUIC congestion control largely copies TCP; the design space for loss detection in QUIC's unique loss recovery framework is barely explored
openings.alien_example: A loss detection: declare loss if (packet_number - last_acked) > (estimated_rtt / min_rtt) * 3 + 2, discovered by simulated annealing

openings.domain: 3D irregular object packing in additive manufacturing (laser powder bed fusion)
openings.objective: maximize packed density within a cylindrical build volume (diameter 250mm, height 325mm) while ensuring no inter-object collision, no overhang >45° without support, and thermal dissipation distance >5mm between parts
openings.space: 10^200+ (continuous rotations + translations for 50+ irregular STL meshes)
openings.value_if_solved: 30-50% reduction in build plate waste; $2B/yr saved in metal AM across aerospace/tooling
openings.neglect_reason: most AM packing optimizers treat 2.5D bounding boxes; true 3D irregular + thermal constraints ignored by industry tools (Materialise, Netfabb)
openings.alien_example: pack a turbine blade, a heat exchanger lattice, and a surgical drill guide into a single cylinder — rotations in 3 axes, concave nesting in blade cavities

openings.domain: scheduling of dynamic wireless power transfer lanes for electric trucks on highways
openings.objective: minimize total energy cost ($) given variable electricity prices, battery state-of-charge, lane availability, and truck arrival times at 200+ charging segments along I-80
openings.space: 10^150+ (assignment of trucks to charging lanes × power levels × time slots over 24h horizon)
openings.value_if_solved: 15-25% reduction in fleet energy costs; enables long-haul EV trucking without massive batteries
openings.neglect_reason: existing DWP scheduling research assumes static demand; real-time lane contention with price dynamics is unaddressed in operations research literature
openings.alien_example: schedule 40 trucks (each with different battery curves) across 12 charging lanes over 2000 miles, where lane activation cost changes every 15min based on grid load

openings.domain: assignment of microreactor experiments to multiwell plates in pharmaceutical high-throughput screening
openings.objective: minimize cross-contamination risk (binary: no reactive pairs adjacent or diagonal) while maximizing well utilization for 1536-well plates with 200+ reagent types
openings.space: 10^400+ (assignment of 200+ reagent types to 1536 wells with adjacency constraints)
openings.value_if_solved: eliminates 5-10% false positives in drug screens; saves $500M/yr in retesting and missed candidates
openings.neglect_reason: commercial plate-filling software (Tecan, Hamilton) uses simple row-wise fill; no combinatorial optimization for reactive adjacency constraints exists in production
openings.alien_example: assign 50 acids, 30 bases, 20 oxidizers, and 100 stable organics to a 384-well plate so no acid-base pair is adjacent — while maximizing replicates per condition

openings.domain: 3D packing of frozen food items into mixed-SKU pallets for cold-chain logistics
openings.objective: maximize pallet utilization (volume %) while respecting tier height limits, weight distribution (CoG within 10% of center), and temperature zone separation (frozen vs. chilled items must be in separate layers)
openings.space: 10^180+ (ordering and orientation of 60+ different SKU boxes per pallet layer, 12-18 layers)
openings.value_if_solved: 8-12% reduction in cold-chain shipping costs; $3B/yr globally in wasted refrigerated truck space
openings.neglect_reason: palletization research focuses on uniform boxes; mixed frozen/chilled with temperature zoning and weight balance is handled manually in warehouses
openings.alien_example: pack 40 boxes of pizzas (-18°C), 30 boxes of ice cream (-25°C), and 20 boxes of yogurt (4°C) onto one pallet with separate thermal layers and stable CoG

openings.domain: routing of autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) in semiconductor fabs with time-windowed overhead hoist transport
openings.objective: minimize sum of lateness penalties (minutes × $/min) for 500+ wafer lots moving between 200+ tools, with collision-free paths and overhead hoist handshake timing constraints
openings.space: 10^300+ (paths for 50+ AMRs × 100+ moves each over 8h shift, with discrete time steps)
openings.value_if_solved: 10-15% increase in fab throughput; $1B/yr per large fab in reduced cycle time
openings.neglect_reason: fab transport optimization treats AMRs and overhead hoists separately; integrated routing with tight handshake timing is NP-hard and unaddressed in commercial MES
openings.alien_example: route 12 AMRs carrying 300mm wafers between 50 tools, coordinating with 20 overhead hoists that must grab at exact ±30s windows — while avoiding deadlocks in narrow aisles

openings.domain: layout of wind turbine positions within a wind farm to minimize wake turbulence losses
openings.objective: maximize total annual energy production (MWh) given 3D terrain, variable wind directions (12 sectors), and turbine-specific power curves with Jensen wake model
openings.space: 10^100+ (continuous (x,y) positions for 50+ turbines in a 10km² area, with minimum spacing constraints)
openings.value_if_solved: 2-5% increase in wind farm output; $500M/yr globally in avoided wake losses
openings.neglect_reason: commercial wind farm design (WindPRO, Openwind) uses gradient-based or grid search; combinatorial optimization with non-convex wake interactions and real terrain is untapped
openings.alien_example: place 80 turbines on a ridgeline with 3 dominant wind directions, such that downstream turbines are never directly behind upstream ones in any sector — while avoiding 5 exclusion zones

openings.domain: packing of irregular 3D medical implants (hip stems, knee trays, spinal cages) into sterilization trays
openings.objective: maximize number of implants per tray (volume utilization) while ensuring ≥2mm gap for steam penetration, no sharp edges touching, and tray weight ≤7kg
openings.space: 10^120+ (6-DOF poses for 20-30 complex titanium implants per tray)
openings.value_if_solved: 20-30% reduction in sterilization cycles; $200M/yr saved in hospital reprocessing costs
openings.neglect_reason: sterilization tray packing is done by hand with foam cutouts; no commercial optimizer handles irregular medical implant geometry with steam gap constraints
openings.alien_example: pack 5 different hip stem sizes, 3 knee trays, and 8 spinal screws into a 600×400×200mm tray, all rotated to nest within each other's concavities with 2mm gaps

openings.domain: assignment of satellite downlink passes to ground stations with weather-dependent signal quality
openings.objective: maximize total data downloaded (gigabytes) over 24h for 100+ LEO satellites, given 30 ground stations with weather-forecasted rain fade (0.1-0.9 probability) and 5-minute pass windows
openings.space: 10^250+ (matching 100+ satellites × 30 stations × 288 5-min slots, with each satellite visible from 2-8 stations per orbit)
openings.value_if_solved: 15-25% increase in satellite data throughput; $1B/yr in improved Earth observation and communications revenue
openings.neglect_reason: satellite scheduling research assumes deterministic link quality; probabilistic weather-aware assignment with combinatorial contention is not solved in commercial (KSAT, SSC) systems
openings.alien_example: schedule 120 satellites (Starlink, Planet, Sentinel) across 30 dishes in Norway/Antarctica/Chile, where rain probability changes every 15min and each satellite has 3-7 possible passes

openings.domain: Acoustic metamaterial unit cells for sub-wavelength sound focusing
openings.verifier: k-Wave (MATLAB/Python) — simulates pressure field through a periodic unit cell; scores transmission/reflection coefficients and focal spot size vs. target frequency
openings.search_space: Continuous geometry of Helmholtz resonators (neck length, cavity volume, wall thickness) + arrangement pattern (hexagonal, square, chiral) + number of resonators per cell → ~10^12 combinations
openings.neglect_reason: Most acoustic metamaterial work uses hand-tuned designs from analytical models; generative design with k-Wave as cheap verifier is rare outside a few niche groups
openings.alien_example: A unit cell with three interconnected spiral channels of varying cross-section, each tuned to a different harmonic, arranged in a quasi-crystalline pattern that focuses 3 kHz sound to a spot 1/20th wavelength wide

openings.domain: Electromagnetic surface lattice absorbers for sub-6 GHz (5G/6G) bands
openings.verifier: openEMS (open-source FDTD) — computes S11/S21 and absorption spectrum over 0.5–10 GHz for a given periodic surface pattern on a grounded dielectric slab
openings.search_space: Topology of conductive patches (shape, split-ring gaps, via positions) + dielectric layer thickness/permittivity + unit cell size → ~10^15 topologies via binary bitmap encoding
openings.neglect_reason: Most metasurface absorbers are designed by intuition or parametric sweeps; generative AI approaches using openEMS as verifier are very sparse (dominated by CST/HFSS commercial users)

openings.domain: acoustic / leaks & faults

openings.sensor: Smartphone MEMS microphone (or cheap electret mic + audio jack)
openings.coupling: Gas escaping at supersonic speed through sub-mm hole generates broadband jet noise (1–50 kHz). Turbulent mixing with ambient air produces characteristic high-frequency hiss that couples directly to the microphone diaphragm via air pressure waves.
openings.verifier: Soap bubble test: spray soapy water on suspected leak; bubbles form exactly where the hiss originates. Record audio near pipe, compute spectral centroid or energy in 15–25 kHz band; compare to known leak vs no-leak spectra.
openings.constructive_use: Early detection of refrigerant leaks in HVAC, natural gas leaks in distribution pipes, or compressed air system leaks—saving energy and preventing hazards, without needing expensive ultrasonic leak detectors.
openings.neglect_reason: Most leak detection uses dedicated ultrasonic gear (>$200) or thermal cameras. Phone mic is ubiquitous but spectral analysis of hiss for sub-mm leaks is rarely attempted; literature focuses on large leaks or correlation methods.
openings.alien_example: Record a 5-second clip near a pipe junction. Run FFT—if energy above 18 kHz exceeds 3× the background, flag as leak. Verify with soap bubbles.

openings.domain: optical / light flicker
openings.signal: AC mains frequency harmonics in LED light output
openings.sensor: phone camera rolling shutter (CMOS sensor)
openings.coupling: LED bulbs driven by AC-DC converters exhibit 100/120 Hz intensity ripple (double mains frequency). Phone CMOS rolling shutter samples this ripple as horizontal banding artifacts; the band frequency encodes mains grid frequency (50/60 Hz) and phase.
openings.verifier: Plug a known AC-powered device (e.g., desk lamp) into same circuit; record simultaneously with a photodiode + oscilloscope (or a second phone with known grid sync) and cross-correlate band spacing to confirmed mains frequency.
openings.constructive_use: Non-contact grid frequency monitoring for power quality assessment, islanding detection in microgrids, or identifying which circuit a device is on without electrical probing.
openings.neglect_reason: Rolling shutter banding is seen as a camera artifact to be removed, not a sensor. No systematic decode of grid frequency from band spacing exists in open literature.
openings.alien_example: Pressing phone camera against a window at night; the banding pattern from distant streetlights reveals if they share a grid phase with your building.

openings.domain: RF / WiFi
openings.signal: WiFi channel state information (CSI) amplitude fluctuations from rotating machinery
openings.sensor: Intel 5300 WiFi NIC with modified driver (or ESP32 with CSI firmware)
openings.coupling: Rotating metal blades (fan, turbine) change the multipath reflection path length at rotation frequency, modulating CSI subcarrier amplitudes at the blade-pass frequency and harmonics.
openings.verifier: Mount a contact tachometer or optical RPM sensor on the machine; compare spectrogram peaks of CSI amplitude time series to confirmed RPM.
openings.constructive_use: Non-contact RPM monitoring of industrial fans, pumps, or motors without attaching sensors; predictive maintenance of rotating equipment.
openings.neglect_reason: CSI is used for human sensing (gesture, gait) and indoor localization; machine vibration sensing via CSI is rare and treated as noise.
openings.alien_example: A WiFi router monitoring a factory fan's health through the wall from 10m away, detecting imbalance before failure.

openings.domain: EM / power
openings.signal: Magnetic field harmonics from switched-mode power supply (SMPS) load changes
openings.sensor: Phone magnetometer (3-axis, ~0.1 μT resolution, 100 Hz sampling)
openings.coupling: SMPS in chargers, computers, and LED drivers draw pulsed current at switching frequency (20-200 kHz) and its harmonics. These create AC magnetic fields that couple inductively to the phone's magnetometer, appearing as low-frequency envelopes when beat against the magnetometer's bandwidth.
openings.verifier: Connect a current probe (e.g., clamp meter with AC output) to the power cord of the device; compare magnetometer FFT peaks to switching frequency calculated from the current waveform.
openings.constructive_use: Identifying device type and operational state (charging, idle, full load) from magnetic signature; energy disaggregation for smart grids without plug sensors.
openings.neglect_reason: Magnetometers are used for compass heading and metal detection. SMPS fields are considered interference to be filtered, not a signal of interest.
openings.alien_example: Walking through an office with a phone; the magnetometer reveals which desks have active laptop chargers and their power states.

openings.neglect_reason: Most research focuses on 2D ground robots or small numbers; 3D swarms with 50+ agents rely on hand-tuned VO parameters, not searched policies

openings.domain: TCP congestion control for datacenter networks
openings.strategy_space: Parameterized AIMD rules (alpha, beta, window scaling, ECN thresholds) or learned congestion window update functions
openings.simulator: ns-3 with a 100-node leaf-spine topology: runs a 10-second flow scenario in ~20 seconds on laptop, scoring flow completion time and throughput fairness

openings.neglect_reason: Most congestion control research uses hand-designed heuristics or complex RL requiring large sim clusters; ns-3 parameter sweeps for novel AIMD variants are underexplored

openings.domain: Auction mechanism for ad slot allocation

openings.simulator: A discrete-event market replay simulator using 1M historical ad requests (from open dataset): runs 10K auction rounds in ~10 seconds on laptop, scoring revenue and advertiser welfare for a proposed mechanism
openings.value_if_found: 5-10% revenue lift over standard GSP or VCG with optimal reserves, with better advertiser satisfaction
openings.neglect_reason: Auction design is dominated by theory or simple experiments; cheap simulation-based search over nonlinear reserve price functions is rare

openings.simulator: A custom Python discrete-event simulator modeling 50 edge nodes with real solar irradiance traces: runs a 24-hour schedule in ~15 seconds on laptop, scoring energy cost and deadline misses
openings.value_if_found: 30% reduction in grid energy consumption with <5% deadline misses compared to EDF or best-fit heuristics
openings.neglect_reason: Most edge scheduling uses fixed heuristics or complex RL; cheap simulation over energy traces for novel heuristic discovery is neglected

openings.domain: Evolutionary heuristics for traveling salesman problem (TSP) crossover operators
openings.strategy_space: Parameterized crossover operators (e.g., edge recombination with adaptive weights, or neural network that selects edges from parents) for TSP instances up to 1000 cities

openings.neglect_reason: Most TSP research uses hand-crafted crossovers; automated discovery of new crossover operators via cheap simulation is rare
openings.alien_example: A crossover that preserves a random subset of edges from one parent and fills remaining cities by solving a small assignment problem

openings.domain: Robotic pushing for object rearrangement
openings.strategy_space: Push parameters (approach angle, velocity, contact point offset) or closed-loop policies for a parallel-jaw gripper pushing objects on a table
openings.simulator: PyBullet with a UR5 arm and 10 random objects: runs a 5-second push sequence in ~5 seconds on laptop, scoring object displacement accuracy and final pose error
openings.value_if_found: 20% improvement in successful object placement over heuristic push strategies (e.g., pushing at center of mass) in clutter
openings.neglect_reason: Most pushing research uses analytical models or RL with thousands of sim hours; cheap simulation search over push strategies is underexplored
openings.alien_example: A strategy that pushes at 15 degrees off-center to induce rotation, then uses the rotation to align the object with a target

openings.domain: Packet routing in wireless mesh networks with dynamic topology
openings.strategy_space: Weight functions for link metrics (ETX, latency, energy) or path selection heuristics for on-demand routing (AODV-style) under node mobility
openings.simulator: ns-3 with 50 mobile nodes in a 500m x 500m area: runs a 60-second mobility scenario in ~40 seconds on laptop, scoring packet delivery ratio and end-to-end delay
openings.value_if_found: 15-25% higher delivery ratio with lower overhead than standard AODV or OLSR under high mobility (5-10 m/s)
openings.neglect_reason: Most mesh routing uses static metrics or complex ML requiring offline training; cheap search over novel metric combinations is neglected
openings.alien_example: A metric that combines ETX with a term penalizing routes that cross areas with recent packet loss bursts, to avoid transient congestion

openings.domain: last-mile drone delivery with heterogeneous landing pad constraints
openings.objective: minimize total energy consumption (Wh) plus landing-wait penalties for a fleet of drones delivering parcels to a set of customer locations, each with a specific landing pad type (flat roof, balcony, garden) that restricts which drone models can land and imposes a time penalty for non-optimal pad use
openings.space: assignment of parcels to drones + ordering of deliveries per drone + selection of landing pad type per stop, with 10-50 drones and 100-500 stops
openings.value_if_solved: 10-30% energy savings and 20% faster delivery times for urban drone logistics companies, enabling same-day delivery at scale
openings.neglect_reason: most drone routing work assumes homogeneous landing pads or ignores pad-type constraints; real-world pads vary widely and are a major operational bottleneck
openings.alien_example: a drone with a wheeled undercarriage can land on a flat roof (0 penalty) but must hover-discharge on a balcony (5s penalty) and cannot land on a garden (skip); a quadcopter can land anywhere but with 10s penalty on slopes

openings.domain: medical drone routing with perishable payload time windows
openings.objective: minimize total flight time (minutes) plus penalty for each unit of payload (e.g., blood, vaccines) that exceeds its temperature-sensitive time window at delivery, computed as a linear decay of payload value after the deadline
openings.space: routing of 5-20 drones from 1-3 depots to 50-200 hospitals/clinics, each with a specific delivery time window and payload type, with drone battery swap at intermediate stations
openings.value_if_solved: reduced waste of perishable medical supplies by 40% and faster emergency response in low-infrastructure regions, saving lives and costs
openings.neglect_reason: most drone routing optimizes for distance or time, not payload decay curves; medical logistics papers focus on truck routing, not drones with battery constraints
openings.alien_example: a blood pack loses 10% value per minute after a 30-minute window; a drone can drop it at a station to extend life by 5 minutes but costs 2 minutes of flight

openings.domain: autonomous vehicle fleet scheduling for on-demand mobility with charging station queuing
openings.objective: minimize total passenger wait time (sum of minutes from request to pickup) plus charging station queue delay (minutes spent waiting for a free charger), computed via a discrete-event simulation of vehicle movements and charger occupancy
openings.space: assignment of 50-500 passenger requests to a fleet of 10-100 autonomous EVs over a 24-hour period, with 5-20 charging stations each with 1-4 chargers, and vehicle relocation decisions
openings.value_if_solved: 15-25% reduction in passenger wait times and 10% fewer charging bottlenecks for ride-hailing companies transitioning to autonomous EVs
openings.neglect_reason: existing AV fleet schedulers treat charging as infinite or ignore queue dynamics; real charging stations have limited spots and cause cascading delays
openings.alien_example: a vehicle with 20% battery must queue for 10 minutes at a station with 2 chargers, causing 3 subsequent pickups to be delayed by 8 minutes each

openings.domain: parcel locker assignment and vehicle routing for multi-modal last-mile delivery
openings.objective: minimize total delivery cost (fuel + driver time) plus locker rental fees, where each parcel is assigned to either a home delivery or a specific locker (with capacity and location), and vehicles route to both homes and lockers
openings.space: assignment of 500-2000 parcels to 50-200 lockers or home delivery, plus vehicle routing for 10-50 trucks, with time windows and locker capacity constraints
openings.value_if_solved: 20-30% cost savings for logistics companies by reducing failed deliveries and optimizing locker utilization, especially in dense urban areas
openings.neglect_reason: most VRP work treats lockers as just extra stops; the combinatorial assignment of parcels to lockers vs. home is rarely optimized jointly with routing
openings.alien_example: a parcel for a customer who is home only 6-8 PM could go to a locker 500m away for $0.50 less, but the locker has only 3 slots left and is on a different truck route

openings.domain: drone swarm coverage path planning for precision agriculture with variable sensor resolution
openings.objective: minimize total flight time (minutes) to cover a set of field polygons, where each polygon requires a specific sensor resolution (e.g., 1cm/pixel for weeds, 10cm/pixel for health) that determines flight altitude and overlap, and drones must return to base for battery swaps
openings.space: partition of field polygons among 2-10 drones + ordering of polygons per drone + altitude selection per polygon, with 20-100 polygons and battery capacity constraints
openings.value_if_solved: 30-50% reduction in survey time and 20% less battery waste for agritech companies, enabling more frequent field monitoring
openings.neglect_reason: most coverage path planning assumes uniform resolution; real ag surveys need variable resolution per zone, and drone battery limits are often ignored
openings.alien_example: a weed-infested zone requires 1cm resolution at 30m altitude (slow, 10 min/km²), while a healthy zone can be 10cm at 100m (fast, 2 min/km²); the swarm must balance battery life across zones

openings.domain: autonomous truck platoon formation and scheduling with mixed traffic on highways
openings.objective: minimize total fuel consumption (liters) across all trucks, where platooning reduces fuel by 10-20% for following trucks, but formation requires matching speeds and meeting points, and trucks have different departure times and destinations
openings.space: scheduling of 20-100 trucks over a highway network (10-30 segments), deciding which trucks form platoons, at which segments, and for how long, with time windows and speed limits
openings.value_if_solved: 5-15% fuel savings for long-haul trucking fleets, translating to millions of dollars annually for large operators, and reduced emissions
openings.neglect_reason: most platoon research assumes all trucks are cooperative and available; real-world scheduling with heterogeneous departure times and destinations is a complex combinatorial problem rarely addressed
openings.alien_example: truck A leaves at 8 AM from NY to Chicago, truck B at 9 AM from Boston to Detroit; they could platoon on I-80 from 10-11 AM if A slows by 2 mph, saving 3 gallons each

openings.domain: electric scooter rebalancing with battery swap station capacity and user demand prediction
openings.objective: minimize total operational cost (truck fuel + driver time + scooter downtime penalty) for redistributing e-scooters across a city to meet predicted demand, where scooters have varying battery levels and swap stations have limited inventory
openings.space: routing of 5-20 rebalancing trucks to pick up/drop off 100-1000 scooters at 50-200 stations, each with battery swap capacity (e.g., 10 batteries), over a 24-hour horizon with hourly demand forecasts
openings.value_if_solved: 15-30% reduction in rebalancing costs and 20% fewer dead batteries for micromobility operators, improving fleet utilization and user satisfaction
openings.neglect_reason: existing rebalancing algorithms treat batteries as uniform or ignore station capacity; real swaps are constrained by inventory and truck capacity
openings.alien_example: a station with 5 full batteries and 10 low scooters can only serve 5 swaps before needing a truck visit; a nearby station has 20 full batteries but low demand, creating a trade-off

openings.domain: last-mile parcel delivery with lockers and crowdshipping integration
openings.objective: minimize total cost (truck fuel + driver time + crowdshipper pay) for delivering parcels to a mix of home addresses, lockers, and crowdshipper handoffs, where crowdshippers are independent drivers with limited capacity and time windows
openings.space: assignment of 500-3000 parcels to delivery mode (home, locker, crowdshipper) + routing of 10-50 company trucks + scheduling of 20-100 crowdshippers, with time windows and capacity constraints
openings.value_if_solved: 20-40% cost reduction for last-mile logistics by leveraging gig economy drivers and reducing truck miles, especially in suburban areas
openings.neglect_reason: most research treats crowdshipping as a separate problem or ignores the joint assignment; the combinatorial integration of three modes is underexplored
openings.alien_example: a parcel for a home 5 miles from the depot could be handed to a crowdshipper already driving that direction for $2, vs. $5 truck cost, but the crowdshipper has only 3 slots and a 2-hour window

openings.domain: Acoustic metamaterial unit cells for sub-wavelength focusing
openings.verifier: k-Wave (MATLAB/Python) simulates wave propagation through periodic unit cells; score = transmission coefficient at focal plane
openings.search_space: Continuous geometry of 2D/3D unit cell (e.g., split-ring, Helmholtz resonator parameters) × lattice periodicity × material density/sound speed
openings.neglect_reason: Most groups hand-design unit cells or use topology optimization on bulk structures; very few explore generative AI over the full unit-cell parameter space with cheap wave solvers
openings.alien_example: A chiral, asymmetric unit cell shaped like a fractal Möbius strip that focuses 10 kHz sound to a spot 0.08λ wide, with negative effective bulk modulus at the focal plane

openings.domain: Microfluidic droplet generator nozzle geometry for monodisperse emulsions
openings.verifier: OpenFOAM interFoam (VOF) on a 2D axisymmetric mesh; score = polydispersity index (PDI) from 10 droplet cycles
openings.search_space: Nozzle cross-section (circle, ellipse, star, spiral slit) × taper angle × surface treatment pattern × flow-rate ratio
openings.neglect_reason: Industry uses standard T-junctions or flow-focusing; lab-on-chip papers vary 1–2 parameters; no one has swept full nozzle morphology with AI-driven search
openings.alien_example: A nozzle with a 3-lobed cloverleaf exit and a counter-rotating inner helix, producing droplets of exactly 12.3 µm at 500 Hz with CV < 0.5%

openings.domain: Dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) shape for wideband 5G mm-wave
openings.verifier: openEMS (FDTD) simulates S11 and gain over 24–40 GHz; score = bandwidth × gain product
openings.search_space: 3D free-form shape (voxel or NURBS) × permittivity (discrete 2–20) × feed position/angle
openings.neglect_reason: DRA design is dominated by canonical shapes (rectangular, cylindrical, hemispherical); generative topology optimization is rare and expensive (CST/COMSOL), but openEMS makes cheap search feasible
openings.alien_example: A toroidal DRA with 6 helical grooves and an off-center coaxial feed, achieving 35% fractional bandwidth with 7 dBi gain, shaped like a cruller donut

openings.domain: Microfluidic chaotic mixer channel pattern for low-Re mixing
openings.verifier: OpenFOAM simpleFoam (steady laminar) with scalar transport; score = mixing index (0–1) at outlet after 20 mm
openings.search_space: 2D channel wall pattern (spline control points, groove depth/width, repetition period) × obstacle shape/position
openings.neglect_reason: Existing mixers are hand-drawn (herringbone, staggered herringbone, Tesla valves); no AI-driven sweep over arbitrary wall patterns with cheap CFD
openings.alien_example: A channel with alternating shark-skin denticles and fractal Koch-curve grooves, achieving 98% mixing at Re=0.1 in 8 mm, with 0.3 psi pressure drop

openings.domain: Thermal metasurface for passive radiative cooling (IR emissivity engineering)
openings.verifier: RCWA (rigorous coupled-wave analysis) via Python (e.g., pyRCWA) or FDTD (openEMS) for spectral emissivity 8–14 µm; score = net cooling power
openings.search_space: Multilayer thin-film stack (material + thickness, 2–10 layers) × 2D grating pattern (period, fill fraction, height)
openings.neglect_reason: Designs are mostly analytical (Bragg mirrors, photonic crystals) or brute-force sweep of 2–3 materials; generative AI over full stack+pattern space is untapped
openings.alien_example: A 7-layer stack of SiO2, Si3N4, and PDMS with a random-dot array on top, achieving 120 W/m² net cooling power under direct sun, with angular selectivity peaked at 45°

openings.domain: Microfluidic paper-based analytical device (µPAD) channel geometry for lateral flow immunoassay
openings.verifier: KLayout + L-Edit DRC rule check + simplified diffusion model (Python PDE solver); score = signal-to-noise ratio at test line after 10 min
openings.search_space: 2D channel layout (width, taper, branches, obstacles, absorbent pad shape) × pore size gradient × reagent deposition pattern
openings.neglect_reason: µPADs are designed by hand or by simple channel-width rules; no one uses generative AI to explore arbitrary channel topologies for optimal flow and binding kinetics
openings.alien_example: A tree-like fractal channel with a spiral delay valve and a porous membrane island, producing 3× stronger signal for 1 ng/mL CRP with 5 min readout

openings.domain: Elastic metasurface for subwavelength vibration isolation (plate waves)
openings.verifier: CalculiX (FEA) or Elmer for harmonic response of thin plate with periodic surface corrugations; score = transmission loss at target frequency band
openings.search_space: 2D surface pattern (indentations, pillars, holes) × unit cell size × material (steel, aluminum, polymer) × pattern symmetry
openings.neglect_reason: Most vibration isolators use mass-spring-damper or bulk phononic crystals; surface-patterned metasurfaces are hand-designed for a few cases; generative search is wide open
openings.alien_example: A plate with a Voronoi-tessellated pattern of conical dimples, creating a 500–800 Hz stop band with 40 dB isolation, only 0.1λ thick

openings.domain: Microfluidic dielectrophoresis (DEP) electrode array for continuous particle sorting
openings.verifier: Elmer (FEM) or openEMS for electrostatic field + particle tracing; score = separation purity for 5 µm vs 10 µm beads at 1 µL/min
openings.search_space: Electrode geometry (interdigitated, castellated, spiral, fractal) × voltage pattern (AC phase, frequency) × channel height × insulator posts
openings.neglect_reason: DEP chip designs are copied from a few canonical patterns (e.g., interdigitated, quadrupole); AI-driven exploration over electrode topology + drive scheme is nearly absent in literature
openings.alien_example: A Sierpinski-triangle electrode array with 3-phase AC drive, creating a rotating field that separates 5 µm, 8 µm, and 12 µm beads into 3 outlets with 99% purity

openings.domain: Power-line vibration
openings.signal: Mechanical vibration of distribution transformers at 100/120 Hz (2× mains frequency) due to magnetostriction
openings.sensor: Smartphone accelerometer (MEMS, ~$0.50 BOM) placed on transformer casing or nearby pole
openings.coupling: Magnetostrictive strain in transformer core at 2× line frequency transfers directly as mechanical vibration through the casing; amplitude modulations encode load current squared
openings.verifier: Clamp-on current transformer (CT) on secondary side; compare RMS vibration amplitude at 100 Hz (FFT peak) vs CT current squared for same 1-minute window
openings.constructive_use: Non-contact load monitoring of residential transformers to detect overload, imbalance, or incipient core saturation before failure
openings.neglect_reason: Vibration monitoring of power transformers is done with expensive IEPE accelerometers ($500+); phone-grade MEMS considered too noisy, yet dithering and synchronous averaging across 10 s yields <5% error
openings.alien_example: A passing truck shakes the pole — subtract its broadband transient via median filtering; the 100 Hz tone survives because it's phase-locked to the grid

openings.domain: Power-line acoustic
openings.signal: Acoustic hum from overhead power lines at 100/120 Hz (corona discharge and conductor vibration)
openings.sensor: Smartphone microphone (MEMS, ~$0.10 BOM) placed 1–5 m from line
openings.coupling: Corona discharge pulses at voltage peaks produce broadband crackle with strong 100 Hz envelope; conductor vibration radiates 100 Hz tone; both modulated by line voltage and surface contamination
openings.verifier: Contact voltage probe on secondary of distribution transformer; compare acoustic 100 Hz amplitude vs RMS voltage over 1 s windows
openings.constructive_use: Detect wet/dry corona, conductor surface degradation, or proximity of vegetation before flashover
openings.neglect_reason: Acoustic line monitoring uses directional microphones arrays ($2000+); phone mic considered too omnidirectional, but time-difference-of-arrival between two cheap mics cancels background hum
openings.alien_example: A bird chirps at 3 kHz — irrelevant; the 100 Hz tone persists; rain increases corona amplitude predictably

openings.domain: Power-line optical (LED flicker)
openings.signal: 100/120 Hz flicker of LED streetlights driven by AC-DC converters with poor ripple rejection
openings.sensor: Smartphone camera rolling shutter (capture 1/4000 s lines) or photodiode (<$1) with audio jack input
openings.coupling: Mains-frequency ripple on LED driver output modulates light intensity at 100/120 Hz; rolling shutter encodes this as alternating bright/dark bands in image; band spacing proportional to frequency
openings.verifier: Oscilloscope across LED driver output (or known 50/60 Hz line frequency); compare band count per frame vs expected 100/120 Hz
openings.constructive_use: Detect failing LED drivers (ripple increases >30%), grid frequency deviation, or phase imbalance from band pattern
openings.neglect_reason: Flicker detection is done with photodiodes and FFT; camera rolling shutter considered a nuisance artifact, not a sensor — yet band spacing gives 0.01 Hz resolution
openings.alien_example: A passing car headlight washes out bands — subtract background frame; the bands reappear because they're phase-locked to AC line

openings.domain: Power-line magnetic near-field
openings.signal: Magnetic field at 50/60 Hz from current-carrying conductors, modulated by load
openings.sensor: Inductor coil (e.g., 10 mH, <$1) connected to smartphone audio input (DC-blocked) as a cheap magnetometer
openings.coupling: Ampère's law: AC current in wire induces voltage in coil proportional to dI/dt; amplitude tracks load current; phase relative to reference gives power factor
openings.verifier: Clamp-on CT on same conductor; compare coil RMS voltage vs CT current over 1 s windows
openings.constructive_use: Non-contact load disaggregation (appliance signatures), detect neutral-ground faults, or monitor arc welder interference
openings.neglect_reason: Magnetic field sensing uses fluxgates ($50+) or Hall sensors; simple inductor considered too crude, but 60 Hz SNR exceeds 40 dB with 1 m coil
openings.alien_example: A nearby transformer's field leaks — subtract a reference coil 1 m away; common-mode cancellation isolates the target wire

openings.domain: Power-line thermal
openings.signal: Surface temperature of distribution transformer casing, modulated by load current squared (I²R heating) and ambient
openings.sensor: Infrared thermopile array (MLX90640, ~$10) or single thermopile ($3) pointed at transformer
openings.coupling: Joule heating in windings conducts to casing; temperature rise ~ I²R * thermal time constant (minutes); ambient temperature adds baseline
openings.verifier: Thermocouple attached to casing (or IR thermometer); compare thermopile reading vs thermocouple every 10 minutes over a day
openings.constructive_use: Predict transformer overload before thermal damage; detect loose connections (hot spots) or cooling fin blockage
openings.neglect_reason: Thermal monitoring uses FLIR cameras ($2000+) or RTDs; cheap thermopile arrays considered low resolution, but 24×32 pixels suffice to spot 5 °C anomalies
openings.alien_example: Sun heats one side — subtract a shaded reference; the load-dependent heating is symmetric and reveals imbalance

openings.domain: Power-line RF (partial discharge)
openings.signal: Radio-frequency bursts (1–100 MHz) from partial discharge in insulation voids, synchronous with AC voltage zero-crossings
openings.sensor: RTL-SDR dongle ($25) with a short whip antenna (1 m) tuned to 40–80 MHz
openings.coupling: Partial discharge creates nanosecond current pulses that radiate broadband RF; pulse repetition rate locks to 50/60 Hz phase angle (e.g., 45° and 135°)
openings.verifier: High-voltage probe on the same cable (or known discharge source like a Tesla coil); compare RF pulse phase vs voltage zero-crossing
openings.constructive_use: Detect incipient insulation failure in underground cables, switchgear, or motor windings before breakdown
openings.neglect_reason: PD detection uses expensive couplers ($5000+) or ultrasonic sensors; cheap SDR considered too noisy, but synchronous averaging over 1000 cycles extracts nV-level signals
openings.alien_example: FM radio station at 88 MHz — notch filter it; PD pulses are 10 ns wide, so they appear as broadband hash only near zero-crossing

openings.domain: Power-line vibration (pole resonance)
openings.signal: Mechanical resonance of wooden utility poles at 10–30 Hz, excited by wind and conductor vibration, damped by soil condition
openings.sensor: Smartphone accelerometer taped to pole at 1.5 m height
openings.coupling: Wind forces excite pole bending modes; conductor vibration at 100 Hz transfers to pole; soil degradation changes damping ratio and resonant frequency (softer soil → lower frequency)
openings.verifier: Soil penetration test (hand auger, cheap) at base; compare measured damping ratio (log decrement from impulse) vs soil moisture/density
openings.constructive_use: Detect rotting pole bases or loose soil before collapse; monitor pole stiffness over seasons
openings.neglect_reason: Pole inspection uses sounding hammers or ground-penetrating radar ($10000); phone accelerometer considered too crude, but 0.1 Hz resolution in damping ratio reveals decay
openings.alien_example: A truck passes — its 2 Hz ground vibration is transient; the pole's 12 Hz ring-down after wind gust is distinct and measurable

openings.domain: Power-line acoustic (insulator cracking)
openings.signal: Audible click or burst at 50/60 Hz from cracked porcelain insulators under wet conditions (flashover precursor)
openings.sensor: Smartphone microphone with parabolic reflector (paper cone, <$1) aimed at insulator string
openings.coupling: Water ingress into crack creates intermittent conduction paths; each half-cycle flashover produces a ~1 ms click at voltage peak; click rate = 100/120 Hz with missing beats
openings.verifier: Visual inspection with binoculars (or drone photo); compare click pattern (missing beats) vs visible crack count
openings.constructive_use: Early warning of insulator failure before catastrophic flashover; prioritize replacement
openings.neglect_reason: Insulator inspection uses UV cameras ($15000) or corona cameras; acoustic clicks considered too faint, but 60 dB gain with reflector yields 10 m detection range
openings.alien_example: Rain creates continuous hiss — clicks are 10 dB above hiss; wind noise is low-frequency (<100 Hz); high-pass filter at 2 kHz isolates clicks

openings.domain: Dynamic EV charging station pricing
openings.strategy_space: Pricing policies (per-kWh price, time-of-day multipliers, congestion surcharges) as functions of grid load, queue length, and battery state-of-charge distribution
openings.simulator: EV-charging-sim (open-source discrete-event simulator: https://github.com/niccokunzmann/ev-charging-sim). Scores a policy by simulating 1000 EVs arriving over 24h with realistic driving patterns, measuring average wait time, total energy delivered, and grid peak load. Runs in ~30 seconds on a laptop.
openings.value_if_found: A pricing heuristic that reduces peak grid load by 20% while keeping average wait under 5 minutes and maintaining station revenue
openings.neglect_reason: Existing work focuses on centralized optimization or simple fixed pricing; heuristic policy search (e.g., genetic programming over decision trees) is almost unexplored
openings.alien_example: A policy that sets price = (queue_length^0.7) * (1 + 0.3*sin(hour_of_day)) * base_rate, discovered by evolution

openings.domain: Home battery arbitrage under TOU tariffs
openings.strategy_space: Threshold rules for when to charge/discharge based on current price, time-of-day, state-of-charge, and forecasted solar generation (e.g., linear or rule-based policies with 5-10 parameters)
openings.simulator: GridLAB-D (open-source distribution system simulator) with a single-home battery model. Scores a policy by running one year of 1-minute resolution data (standard TOU tariff, real solar irradiance trace). Runs in ~2 minutes on a laptop.
openings.value_if_found: A simple 3-parameter policy that achieves >90% of theoretical optimal arbitrage profit (vs. perfect foresight dynamic programming)
openings.neglect_reason: Most work uses MPC or RL; simple interpretable heuristic policies for home batteries are underexplored despite being deployable on cheap microcontrollers
openings.alien_example: Charge if (price < 0.08 $/kWh AND soc < 0.9) OR (soc < 0.3 AND hour between 10-14); discharge if (price > 0.25 AND soc > 0.2)

openings.domain: Thermostat setpoint scheduling for demand response
openings.strategy_space: 24-hour setpoint schedules (hourly values) or piecewise-linear functions with 4-8 breakpoints, parameterized by outdoor temperature forecast and occupancy pattern
openings.simulator: EnergyPlus (open-source building energy simulation) with a single-zone residential model. Scores a schedule by simulating one day and measuring peak power reduction vs. comfort violation. Runs in ~1 minute on a laptop.
openings.value_if_found: A 6-parameter schedule that reduces peak HVAC load by 35% while keeping temperature within ±1°C of comfort band for 95% of occupied hours
openings.neglect_reason: Demand response research focuses on price signals or direct load control; automated discovery of simple setpoint heuristics is overlooked
openings.alien_example: Pre-cool to 20°C at 14:00, ramp to 24°C at 17:00, recover to 22°C by 19:00, with ramp slope proportional to outdoor temperature

openings.domain: Water distribution network valve scheduling
openings.strategy_space: Valve open/close schedules (binary decisions per valve, 24 hourly steps) as a function of tank levels and time-of-day, represented as decision trees or rule sets
openings.simulator: EPANET (open-source water distribution simulator). Scores a schedule by simulating 24h hydraulic behavior, measuring pressure violations, water age, and pump energy. Runs in ~10 seconds on a laptop.
openings.value_if_found: A 5-rule decision tree that reduces pump energy 15% while maintaining pressure above 30 psi at all nodes
openings.neglect_reason: Water network control uses optimization or model predictive control; heuristic rule discovery is rare despite operator preference for interpretable rules

openings.domain: Congestion-aware routing for parcel delivery drones

openings.domain: Induction motor winding health

openings.coupling: Turn-to-turn short in stator winding creates local circulating current loops; these produce a magnetic field component at 2× line frequency (120 Hz) that is phase-shifted relative to the main field, detectable as a change in the ratio of 120 Hz to 60 Hz in the magnetometer FFT.
openings.verifier: Measure actual winding resistance with a cheap multimeter ($10) at motor terminals; a resistance drop of >3% from baseline indicates shorted turns. Compare FFT harmonic ratio to resistance reading.

openings.domain: Transformer core saturation detection

openings.verifier: Measure primary current with a $20 clamp meter; compare THD (total harmonic distortion) from coil vs clamp meter current THD.

openings.alien_example: Wrap relay coil around transformer leg, connect to microphone input, record 10 s. Compute FFT, measure ratio of 180 Hz to 60 Hz. Ratio >0.05 indicates saturation onset.

openings.domain: Battery internal resistance from magnetic field ripple

openings.domain: Soil moisture via earth's magnetic field attenuation
openings.signal: Amplitude of 60 Hz power-line magnetic field at ground level
openings.sensor: Smartphone magnetometer (3-axis, 10 Hz sample rate)
openings.coupling: Moist soil has higher electrical conductivity (0.01–0.1 S/m) than dry soil (10⁻⁴ S/m). The 60 Hz field from power lines induces eddy currents in the ground; these secondary fields oppose the primary, reducing total field amplitude measured 1 m above ground. Wet soil → more attenuation.
openings.verifier: Take a soil sample at the measurement point, weigh it wet, oven-dry it, and compute gravimetric moisture content. Compare to magnetometer amplitude reading.
openings.constructive_use: Irrigation scheduling for agriculture — map soil moisture across a field without burying sensors.

openings.alien_example: Stand at a fixed GPS point under a power line, hold phone flat at 1 m height, record magnetometer for 30 s. Extract 60 Hz amplitude via FFT. Repeat after rain; amplitude drop correlates with moisture increase.

openings.constructive_use: Non-destructive evaluation of concrete bridge decks, parking garages, and seawalls for rebar corrosion before spalling occurs.

openings.domain: Acoustic + Vibration
openings.signal: Acoustic emission (AE) from a stressed bolt detected by a piezo disc
openings.sensor: Piezoelectric disc (e.g., 27 mm diameter, ~$1) glued to bolt head
openings.coupling: A tightening bolt under torque undergoes plastic deformation at the thread root, emitting burst AE signals (100-500 kHz). The number of AE hits per 10° rotation correlates with incipient yielding (torque-tension nonlinearity).
openings.verifier: Torque wrench + digital caliper measuring bolt elongation; compare cumulative AE hits vs. torque-angle curve. Checked with load cell.
openings.constructive_use: Real-time detection of bolt yielding during assembly in automotive or aerospace, preventing over-torque without expensive ultrasonic bolt tension monitors.
openings.neglect_reason: AE sensing is used for crack growth in large structures, but using a $1 piezo disc to detect bolt yielding during tightening is neglected because the signal is buried in mechanical noise (wrench clicks).
openings.alien_example: An AI could train a 1D autoencoder on the raw AE waveform from a healthy bolt, then flag anomalous bursts during tightening that indicate plastic deformation before the torque-angle curve flattens.

openings.domain: supply-chain inventory replenishment heuristics

openings.neglect_reason: most supply chain literature uses hand-tuned (s,S) or simple base-stock; deep RL is too expensive and overkill; AI search over parametric heuristics is barely explored

openings.domain: priority queue scheduling in network routers (active queue management)
openings.strategy_space: all possible drop/mark probability functions of queue length, arrival rate, and recent loss history (e.g., RED variants, neural AQM, piecewise-linear curves, fuzzy rules)

openings.neglect_reason: AQM research mostly hand-tunes RED parameters or uses simple PI controllers; black-box policy search is rare
openings.alien_example: a mark probability = 0.5 * (queue_len/100)^1.5 * (1 + 0.1*sin(arrival_rate*0.1))

openings.domain: auction bid shading heuristics for display advertising
openings.strategy_space: all possible shading functions that map (expected value, competition intensity, remaining budget, time) to a multiplicative bid factor between 0 and 1
openings.simulator: ad-exchange replay simulator: given a shading function, replay 100,000 auction logs (public from iPinYou/Yahoo), compute profit = (value - cost) * win. Scores in ~30 seconds on a laptop.

openings.domain: adaptive backoff algorithm for wireless sensor network MAC protocols
openings.strategy_space: all possible backoff functions of (number of recent collisions, channel load estimate, remaining energy) that determine next backoff window size
openings.simulator: ns-3 or OMNeT++ simulation of a 50-node sensor network with Poisson traffic: given a backoff function, run 60 seconds, score = packet delivery ratio / average latency. Scores in ~15 seconds on a laptop.

openings.neglect_reason: most WSN MAC uses fixed BEB or simple linear adjustments; learned backoff is rare

openings.domain: evolutionary crossover/mutation operator selection for genetic algorithms on combinatorial optimization

openings.neglect_reason: most GA research uses fixed operators or simple adaptive schemes; full policy search over operator choices is neglected

openings.domain: cache eviction policy in content delivery networks (CDN)
